degmeic chiantestaig Ch., Caithr. Thoirdh. 3.2.

eg.p:
= testugad (2 testaigid) and testáil: ar tesdadh don
ridiri sin (testail v.l.)
when that knight died, ITS xix 14.10.

form.p: g (teist)

eg.p:
(a) bears witness, testifies, affirms: ro-
thestaig o luga, co tibred anoir ... do, PH 6621. t. in bo
aire test ┐ antest do chenelaib echtrann cen fír, H.5.15, 23a
(O'D. 1659).

(b) tests, tries: in inbuid ro testuig in mainniur `tried
it,' Laws ii 54.7 Comm. bean do theastaigh an raon rompa,
PBocht 9.10. ro testaigit a tren-fir, MR 140.6. ní bhfuil
dlighe ná gaois ná gárda | ... | nár theastaidh
which he did
not put to the proof, Hackett xl 92. teastuighim na bealaighe
go minic dom chois, Ó Bruad. iii 6.13. teastuighid forr-
dhubha a shúl clann na ndaóine, Ps. xi 4.

form.p: Vn. testugad.

egForm.p:
(a) bearing witness, testifying: fiadnaise
don eclais for a manchaib ... ┐ for cach tuata uile cid saer-
manach he, muna raib eclais aile aca testugud `claiming
him,' Laws ii 346.2 Comm. is emalta lais an ughdar beith
do gres ag testugadh .i. dliged nad beir do cum fir dé, Eg.
88, 49 (50)d (O'C. 2587). na fiadhuin dia thestu[ga]dh
iartain `attest,' Laws i 300.34 Comm. senoir sruith lais ...
dia theastugud fiadh Romanchu, Lism. L. 217.

eg.p:
(b) testing, trying: ar a met rob fhaill do can a teg do
testugadh, Laws iii 276.x Comm. urchur testai[g]thi
`trial throw' (Gloss.), v 140.14 Comm. iar testu[gad] na
teiti `having tested the rope,' 238.15 Comm. do th. a
tapaid, MR 198.15. ? Here also: co risiur nem ... | iar
testugud na teora, Rawl. 69b51.

form.p: g (do-esta, testa)

eg.p:
(a) is lacking, wanting: in
taiscidh tucadh na láim nach tesdobadh, Caithr. Thoirdh.
93.z. an tan nach dtasduighe ann aon-choinghioll, Donl.
278.11. an tan do thasduigheas, 318.6. tál nach teastuigh
`tide which knows no ebbing,' Ó Bruad. ii 72.20. Usually with
ó of person from whom someth. is lacking: ni theisdeobha
enní uadha, BNnÉ 230 § 136. ní theistteóbhaid na neithe
bheas 'na riachtanas oirn ... uainn, Desid. 4476. in tan
theasdaigheas bó uait, Oss. v 12.11. muna tteasduighe
encomartha acu so uadha, 23 K 42, 224.z.

(b) dies: conerbailt (.i. testaig) sochaide mor dib, Arch.
iii 18.2. do testuidur moran dona pagánachaib, Fier. 215.
dia tesdaidi oglach cin sheitig, Marco P. 38. san mbliadhain
roimh ocht is ocht | teastaigh an t-uasal éadtrocht, Ó Bruad.
iii 56.14. ata a naicid nach testuigenn co luath = vitam
pollicentur, Rosa Ang. 196.16. testaighi in fiabrus ┐ fer in
fiabrusa an enfhecht, RC xlix 13.10.

Vn. testáil. Also testugad: diongmhalta, iomlan, gan
einní dá dhí[th] nó dá theasdughadh, Eg. Gl. 211.

form.p:
f. Late vn. of do-esta and 2 testaigid (see tesbaid).
In syll. verse also teasbháil. tesdáil, tesbháil, IGT Decl.
§ 148.

eg.p:
(a) a being lacking, wanting; lack, want: ná bac
dá dteasda teasdáil, DDána 53.22. ? ceist dot' theastaluibh
curach ... d'fagāil (? leg. cheastuibh, Gloss.), Feis TC 912.

(b) act of dying: a n-gabail ... do mac rig Saxan ... ┐ a
tesdail aige, AU ii 512.3. Aedh ... ri Ailig do tesdail a n-ais
foirbthi, RC xvii 374.16. suil fríoth fios a theasdála, DDána
86.11. re hucht dteasdála, Aithd. D. 10.32. ar bheith
dheit ┐ tú ar dteasbháil (: deasláimh) `after Thy death,'
73.13. C. ... do theastail do heircc siabhorghaloir, Ériu
iv 64.1. an fedann neach tesdail is na fiabrusaib gera,
RC xlix 31.7.

egForm.p:
i (teist) famous, renowned: in trinóit t., Thes.
ii 351.43. na trenfher t., TTr. 1396. mileda rochalma
rotestamla na Troiándae, TTr.² 1600.

i (teist) testimony, witness: dosberam testamla
maithe fort i fhiadnaise phopuil I.
we will speak well of you,
LB 151a58.

(? teist): tri maic Dorchlaim, tromm t. `strong
testimony,' Met. Dinds. iii 52.45 (: chestach, but perfect
rhyme not essential here. ? Leg. testach. See note).

form.p: u (in Mod. Ir. also o), m. (teist)

eg.p:
(a) testimony, witness:
do thabirt testassa airibsi `to give evidence for you,' Wb
16a26. testis (? leg. testus) .i. fiadhnaise, Laws i 292.30
Comm. testus necomlán .i. rainaic cu ruice an inad i
nebairt beith, ┐ ni fagaib a teist do tabairt co comlán,
H.3.18, 296 (O'C. 607). guth ind athar ... ic tabairt
chaintestusa arin mac, LB 107a24. t. Heleráin for Patraic,
Trip. 550.31. dodeochaid senoir ... leis o G. fria imcomet
┐ fri testus, Anecd. iii 31.11. na hóga nach forcoimetat
demin[t]estus in choimded (sic leg.), Thr. Hom. 52.2. sin
do thabhairt mar theastas air, TSh. 9831. ag cur teastais
na muinntire seo síos ar Éirinn, Keat. i 10.38.

(b) praise, fame, reputation: ingnad testas (sic leg.) |
cathrach ara mbi a breat[h]aga, Arch. iii 235 § 20. cāin-
testus a laechradh, 294 § 5. id cháithréim theastais
in your
famed triumph, Hackett xx 53. an bhé chliste is fearra
tréithe agus teastas `in virtue and fame,' ITS iii 170.35.
see teistimin.
see teistiu.
see tesmailt.

form.p:
ā, f. IGT Decl. § 39 (91.6). Also o, m., § 62. np. -theoit,
Ériu iv 96 § 15 v.l. teóid, IGT Decl. ex. 1477. ds. lé téd,
Josh. ii 15.

eg.p:
(a) rope, cord: t. gl. fidis, Sg. 46b7. cneslénti (sic leg.)
... bítís bá thétaib ┐ rothaib ┐ refedaib hi cústul fri gelcnes
dó, LU 6413. di thétaib ┐ refedaib in carpait, 5187. tetim-
nech na t., CRR 54.7. i crithnugud clár ┐ táet ┐ tili, TTr.
1346. eirridecht co tri fa tetaib .i. a eirridecht do denum
do co tri tetaib fai .i. tet ana gabul ┐ tet ceachtar do da
(sic) ladhair, ┐ dul do ar in fairrgi amlaid sin (of a warrior),
23 P 3, 21 (23)a (O'C. 1875). a suainemnaib na teite `by
the strings of the rope,' Laws v 238.15 Comm. da théit,
Lism. L. 4833. téada na bpeacadh funes peccatorum, TSh.
7481.

egForm.p:
(b) string of a stringed instrument: na deichtétae gl.
decim chordarum, Ml 51c4. crott deichde .i. co tairissedar
o deich tétaib, Hib. Min. 20. téta mendchrot, LU 7019.
crot ... cen choe astuda a t. ... ainm don delgain bic fostas
in teit humaide na crute, RC xx 164-6 (ACC) = LU 617 ff.
téda do chroinn, Studies 1919, 611 § 3. lucht téad,
Dánfhocail 163. lá fear téd ultach, FM iv 1184.8 .i.
clairseoir, note. aos teud `musicians,' Keat. i 70.59. Cf.
téd nomen de sono factum, Corm. 42 = Corm. Y 1211.
tet timpan, ACC (Lib. Hymn.) 647. tét .i. tiompán, O'Cl.

eg.p:
(c) a spider's thread: téd an damháin ealluidh, Mac
Aingil 182.13.

egForm.p:
Compds. bind of sweet strings, sweet as music, tuneful:
oc Túaig théit-bind, Met. Dinds. iv 60.34. sluag ... teidbind,
YBL 163b15. corab t. ... a mínchomrad, Aisl. MC 97.18.
ceolu teitbindi, Ériu ii 126.x. an tiompán téad-bhinn,
ML 50.8. binde sweetness of strings: mo thimpán co
téidbinne, SG 248.37. bindes = binde: teidbindeas ciuil,
BB 42b14. lucht ted-bhinniosa ciuil, Geneal. Tracts i
21.14. chless rope-feat (one of Cú Chulainn's accomplish-
ments): tétcless, TBC 2100 (see n. p. 280). chrot
stringed harp: a dtéidchrot meann `harp-strings,' TD 35.8.
gel: téitgel triathglan ... E. `E. of the white rigging, a
bright lord,' Arch. Hib. ii 70 § 5. lebar having slender
strings: an liric ... téidleabhair, Studies 1923, 598 § 9.
long rigged ship: ina thétluing, Arch. Hib. ii 70 § 3.
refed rope: tet-réfed rofada, CCath. 3324. téittréfedh
rofoda, Hugh Roe 14.3.

(cf. te) wanton: mac t., Ériu iii 135.4. Superl. cía
tétem rangais? `who are the most wanton?,' Tec. Corm.
p. vi.

(? cf. sét) road, way: tet .i. slige, RC xx 412.12 (ACC).
o tharrastair ... int en con nem-cumscaigthe for in tet, YBL
165a27 (cf. conair, 25).

eg.p: t. .i. tuath thíre. téte .i. tuatha, O'Cl.

lán ind árim na .vii. bliadna ar díb cétaib | gabsat
cocad re ṅgein I. martétaib, LL 35b38.

egForm.p:
In compds., meaning uncertain. Perh. warm, hot,
furious, etc. (cf. te, 2 tét). ádbul: ri rodelb t. De | do
chetadbur na ndule | ... | in mass amra écruthach, SR 21.
ag furious (?) stag: ba samalta ... ra tetag n-allaid arna
chetgluasacht do chonaib, TBC 3382. balc: nir thessaigh
a treb toettbailc | acht Cesair, Leb. Gab. 92.28 = tetbailc,
LL 6b37 `her very powerful household,' ITS xxxix 167.
béim: fuamnaigfiter sluaig | dia tibra tét-béimenn, SG
321.13. blai: frisin tetblai (: cetna) (of the lawn of
heaven), SR 407. ? brug: [n]imthang tadg torbathar |
testidib tétbroga, IT iii 35.4 (tesdib teobrogha, v.l.).
buillech: Domnall diubartach tabarthach tetbuillech,
Anecd. ii 65.2. gorm: contuil in t. co thich | dia luid éc
éclond Using, LL 133a24. mall: a ri in tormgloir tetmaill,
IT iii 73. 16 (? compd. of 1 tét).

o, ā (1 tét) stringed. As subst. (ā, f.): tall a ochtte-
daich ... chuicci ... ┐ rosephaind ceōl
his eight-stringed
instrument, ZCP v 500.10.

o, ā=2 tét: tédach .i. merugadh, ut est, bai mac
tédach laisin ríg, H.3.18, 627 (O'C. 1374) =mac tét, Ériu
iii 135.4. ? tedaidh .i. mear, O'Cl. See also taetach.

eg.p: see titacht.

egForm.p:
io,m. (1 tét) harper, lute-player: fidicen. tédaire,
Ir. Gl. 1017.

o, m. (1 tét) rope, cord: birt troma i dtéadánaibh
`in corded bundles,' TD 16.59.

dered dind ló. cromm barr cráeb. ísel t. fidbad, RC
xiv 418.z (? leg. cetar, Stokes). ? Leg. tetarfidbad `inter-
vening
forest', Plummer MS. notes.

o, m. vn. of do-etarcuirethar act of interposing :
cen t. drogimrato, Wb 3d5.

form.p:
vn. of do-etarrat. This form serves as ds., but
in Mid. Ir. nds. also tetarrachtain.

eg.p:
(a) pursuing, overtaking, catching: ic t. Rúaid co rinn,
Met. Dinds. ii 30.63. undsea chethirn ṅgilla ... anair da
tetarrachtain, TBC 5764. luid Finn ... do thetar[r]acht ale
for Currech `to seize,' RC xiv 242.9. do chóidh co ndirim
móir marcslóigh ... dia ttéttarrachtain, FM vi 1978.8. laa
chaidchi do Guaire oca th. ┐ ni ruba fer dia muinter (of a
game of chess), Ériu v 32.24. dogní cuthig ... | ...dia th.
`to catch himself,' Met. Dinds. iv 122.x. Cf. teadarracht .i.
dioghail, O'Cl.

(b) encompassing, bringing about: doratsat uile a men-
main fri t. a marbtha, TTr.² 1550. do thetarrachtain a
chind do bualad dar bil in sceith ar n-uachtar, Mann. and
Cust. iii 448.12. ní da thetarrachtain gaili na gascid berair
in rumpud sin, MU 34.17. ra thaegat ass ... do thetarractain
al lama d'fhurdergad re cach
that they might succeed in,
TBC 5098. Cf. ba tetarrachtain dóib, cia dib no bérad a
chétguine fair
they vied with each other as to which ...,
679. Hence with baegal: do thetarreacht ar mbaegail
to take us by surprise, Anecd. i 5.10. batar an dí shochraide
occ tettarrochtin boeghail aroile, Hugh Roe 152.15. gan
beith dogres acc téttarractain baoghail gabhála ... for an
bport sin, FM vi 2034.15.

in tan conaitecht don tuisiuch fria toil tetath |
asbert itir nochon fitir pecadh bétach, Anecd. i 62 §
101.

(?compd. of 1 tét): nis foelsat a tetbannai
(: rétlannai) (of falling stars), SR 8163. airgit aní ro bói
and | co n-ilur tuarad tetband, IT iii 526.886. ni meirb
dofich Falbe Flann | frisloisc fiena a t[h]ētbann `the play
of his spear-strings withers the host,' Fianaig. 12 § 17. Cf.
Tigernach Tétbannach, LU 10712.
see téite.

t. co raoind cuid fearda aenfer dan do dimnidi,
BB 380a51.

form.p:
iā, f. n. loc. of a district comprising parts of West-
meath and Longford, Teffia: nom. Tethbe, Hog. Onom.
Tethba, Met. Dinds. iv 230.1. acc. Tethbai, Trip. 86.12.
Tethba, LL 6a36. gen. Tethbe, Hog. Onom. Tethbae, AU
i 120.9. Tethba, 72.12. Tebhtha, ZCP xx 5.2. Theaftha,
Lec. 60a2. Tethbai, AU i 344.12. LU 10714. dat. Tethbai,
AU i 344.2. LU 10714. Tebtha, AU i 554.1. Tethfa, Lec.
60a5. In du. i Cenánnas etir di Thethba, Trip. 518.40.
Cf. in duas Tethbias, Thes. ii 264.27. do ... Tethbhaibh,
FM ii 670.8. See ZCP xx 1 ff. JRSAI lxviii 241 ff. lxxi
101 ff. Ériu xiii 88 ff. Wortk. 23.

eg.p:
Also of eponym of Teffia: dorat Tethba don tír thúaid, |
... | a comainm clethach, Met. Dinds. iv 230.1.

t. .i. titan .i. grian, O'Cl. ? Cf. a delb amail thēthein
tra `like a fiery blaze,' Otia ii 88.13.
see 1 teinnid.
trega t. temidi, BB 380b2.

egForm.p:
scaldcrow, (?) war-goddess: t. ar bháidhbh, Met.
Gl. 11 § 14. teathra .i. badhb no feanóg, O'Cl. dobeir
tomra do t[h]ethraibh, Sitzb. 1919 v 92 § 11. dorat ... |
colt do t[h]ethraib, § 12. ? Cf. mían mná Tethrach .i. badb,
LU p. 124 n. (see 3 tethra). ? teidm t. `deadly plague,'
RC xiv 418.2.

(? same wd. as prec.) paragon: C. ... tetra Erenn
etir guth ┐ cruth ┐ soas, AU i 444.15 (.i. cantaire no orator,
FM ii 608.14). teathra Erenn bheós ar chruth, ar chéill,
1008.8. ? To this: bat firen firbrethach cen forbrisiu
n-indsciu etir tethrai tren ┐ trug, Ériu viii 173.20.

eg.p:
(a) the sea: ? tethrach .i. traigh, ut est ro fine
tonn tethrach .i. ro traighi tonn taitnemach na fine amail
é (`the wave of the family has ebbed'), O'Dav. 1562 (taken
by Stokes as redupl. perf. of tráigid, cf. ZCP xvii 154.3 and
tethraigid). teathra .i. muir, O'Cl. t. ar dtuile `a sea that is
poured forth as a flood,' O'Gr. Cat. 491.4. Grecca nostiad
tar t. (gl. tar muir), Leb. Gab. 108.13.

(b) n.pr. of a Fomorian king, see ZCP xi 182 f.: T. .i.
ainm rīg Fomore ut est isin Imagallaim in dā Thūar: iter
trīuna Tethrach, Corm. Y 1207 =Tethru, Corm. Bodl. 44 =
RC xxvi 26 § 97. do ingentib inad Tetrach rig Fomorie,
ZCP iii 234.10. as i an moir Mag Tetrai (.i. ri di rigaib)
Fomore Tethrai .i. mag rig Fomóre, 240.3. triath tiri
Teathrach .i. Muredhach, Anecd. ii 52.2. cia buar Tethrach
tibiti, IT iii 61.20. mían mná Tethrach (.i. badb) a tenid,
LU p. 124 n. ? To this: damh Smirgaill mic Teathrach,
Met. Dinds. iv 302.17 = Comp. Con. C. 37.16. Of a woman:
T. bán-gel ba ben Chorrginn, Met. Dinds. iv 108.23.

Various unclassified exx.: t. t. da lua, LU 10255
=tetra tetrai, ZCP iii 234.18. adh aghad re theatra ┐ ni
diultaig dhi no go cuirthear a naon uaigh iat ar aon, Eg. 88
fo. 23 (24)b (O'C. 2307). gell fēile ... | atā anosa ag ūibh
Eachach, | ni tēit tethro 'na mbronntoib, Sitzb. 1919
v 92 § 2. atcobrai cech tethrai .i. ben, Hib. Min. 47.24.

egForm.p:
o, ā tir t. (: Bethrach), SR 978. atecha Temair
tetraigh, LL 393b24. Temraich tethraigh torachtu, BB 380b9.
? oc temair truim tetorig, ZCP viii 306.26. cen tim timine
tethiguth tethrig, 16. See also ZCP xvii 154.2 s.v. teth-
raigid.

g ro tetraig .i. ro forbair, RC xxi 401.17 (? cf. 2
tethra). dolluid adollus ara thethraig a nert nach ṅderbai
dia chéim (Nuallguba Emire), LL 123a41. ? nir ro selgatar
amal lighes milchobur mil millsiund sastund sálmara móir
tethragtar cutig, 116a48. do laith lochrann talmhan
tethraigh mara mos-tire-timchealla tethraigh tráighes
láthrach, ZCP xvii 154.2. See 3 tethra (a).

eg.p: see téitimnech.

egForm.p:
vn. of do-etla (see under téltóg). stealing, carrying off:
tlenamain .i. doetlo ... .i. ar t. a cétmuinntire dia cinn,
O'Dav. 1553. See tothla.

trí buadnasa t., Triads 88 v.ll. (trí buada téiti
`three glories of a gathering', text).

o, ā (1 tét) tuneful, melodious. Superl.: an
chōra cheōilbhinn ... [ba] chaointētnamaighi ... isan crīs-
taigheacht uile, Fl. Earls 184.12.

ā, f. and o, m. (cf. 6 tét) violence, roughness, fury:
teadnas (tédnas) .i. burba, no mearrdhacht, O'Cl. U. triana
thétnais tind | atá 'n écmais a cháil-chind, Met. Dinds.
iii 98.29. is imda écht ar bith bras | iarna dénum tria th.,
iv 134.2. dognitis tetnais co trén, Rawl. 77a10. nár thuiti
i tétnais, SG 365.12. tir ... cin coibnesta, acht tetnuis ┐
burba, Laws iv 26.19 Comm. an gach tethnais `during
violence,' 268.17. Of horses: tetnuis .i. merechduin
`excitement, rustiness of a horse,' O'Don. Suppl. (from
H.3.18). is īc a cinad (sic leg.) is in tetnais fair `in its
violence,' Laws iii 180.11 Comm. Note also: ar a thednus
fri olcus `for his opposition to evil,' O'Don. Gr. 297 Hard.²
296.6.

o, ā (tétnas) violent, furious: ina treibh tetnasaigh
laidir, Leb. Gab. 92 n. 7 (in gl. on toettbailc).

eg.p:
da derbrathair thētraide (: sētglaine) (of Gad
and Asher, Gen. xxx 11-13) Rawl. 72b44.
see técs.
see tecsaid.

egForm.p:
f. ? (cf. fortí chóir, LU 7079). np. tii, IT iii 239.136.
cloak: tī .i. brat, Corm. Y 1199. ti .i. brat, ut est domicfa
t. mo macain, O'Dav. 1555. dopheir a t. fon tsali, RC xi
129.12. ti dubglas co luban airgid, YBL 136a46.

form.p: f. np. tithe, Corm. Y 607.

egForm.p:
(a) line, circle: cuires ... ti dia bhachaill a ttimcheall an
bhuair, BNnÉ 185.29. fuair bas iar tteacht tar an tt. dó,
31. co tabair t. dia erbull impu, RC xx 410.2. títhe im
ghruaidh `furrows,' Hackett xix 12. Of the lines on a
chess-board: is cethrachair cētumus ind fithchill ┐ it dīrge
a tīthe, Corm. Y 607. dias dub damsa im en fer fhind duidseo
forsin nentí, Ériu v 32.21. tú, a rígh Bhredh, ar an tt.
thall | as fer ar gach t. ad tiomchall, TD ii 198.36.

(b) in pl., space enclosed by lines, `fines,' surface: títhe
orláir do ghruadh ngeal, Studies 1921 74 § 6. ní lingfidhir
títhe cláir Chraoi Chonchobhair, DDána 109.19. saoir-
thíthe chóig ccoigedh, Bk. of O'Conor D. 297b16.

eg.p:
(c) spot : dá bfaghbar ... éntí fholaimh at ghnúis, O'Gr.
Cat. 456.5. an t. ghlas ní dheachaidh de, Keat. ii 306.
croicne leoman ngel ┐ dub ┐ derg ina tithib, ZCP i 380.12
títhe dearga o thrágh go tráigh, Rel. Celt. ii 224.30.

(d) preceded by the preposition for, later ar, pursuing,
attacking, attempting to, about to: mong .i. mo ... a fochaidhe
.i. maile no leithe no cutum for a thi, Corm. Y 935. beth
for th. na ndaine seo, Laws v 160.14 Comm. isat marba in
lucht batar ar bar tíi, LB 143b26. ecc ro pa truacch ara t.,
FM ii 898.14. sé's an talamh ar t. a chéile, PBocht 10.3.
do bhí H. ar a th.-sean, Mark vi 19. léim ar th. `léim tar
tórainn ?' (note), Dán Dé xv 20. atá teaghlach a thighe
| ar t. tuillidh muinntire
seeking increase, xxi 29. ná bí
ar t. chagaidh ar chlog, Studies 1924, 244 § 27. tillid airg-
theóiridhe ... dá dtigh ar t. fillte go grod tar a n-ais post
non longum tempus reversuri, Keat. ii 6123. tarla an mac
... na dhalta ... ag Ciarán ar t. bheith na mhanach, iii 825.
do bhíodh a thoil ar t. a dáilte `ready to be bestowed', Studies
1919, 75 § 20. ar t. síothchána do cheangal, TSh. 3834.

Cf. doraind Pátraic Ráith nAirthir a bachaill buan tith,
Trip.² 754. techta .i. ti ichta uair t. riagail, Cóic Con.
Fug. 29 § 14.
see í.
see í.

egForm.p:
o, m. (Téib) a Theban: Craidhon ri na Tiabha-
nach, St. Ercuil 18. co ndechudar ... ┐ na Tiabhanaigh
isin Teibh, 741.

[io, iā (Téib) Theban: don chiniud thromglan
Tiabanda, TTebe 226. na rig tromglana Thiabanda, 82.
As subst.: cathugud mor na Tiabhanta, 6.

(a) sharp, grievous: tiachair ┐ serb, Ml 94c6.
tichair lainn, gl. hic acer, Sg. 41a10. serb no tiachair, O'Dav.
1030. tiachair .i. feargach no teinn, O'Cl. ba tiachair le a
cenn, Lism. L. 1383. in gním talchair tiachair, Met. Dinds.
iii 408.3. As subst.: nír airigh ... doigh na tiachair, BNnÉ
101.33. Later diachair: peannaid ná pian ná diachair
bháisbhruid, ITS iii a 104.60. diachair `sorrow, grief',
O'R.

eg.p: (b) clever, prudent: tiachair .i. glic, O'Dav. 441.

Compd. thaeb wounded in the side : atú tursech tiachar-
thaeb, TBC 2330.

form.p: [iā,f.] (tiachair).

eg.p:
(a) pain, grief: corḟácaibh fo th. F., Met. Dinds. iv 72.55.
tiachra inna lám-chomart `affliction of hand-smitings,'
Ériu ii 136 § 120. roruamnai(g)set a naighthi la tiachra,
TTr.² 1578. mar tiachra .i. moran galair, ZCP v 487 § 1.

(b) prudence, cunning: dorindnacht la suithi | soas co
ṁméit tiachrai, Fél. Nov. 12. tiachrai .i. glicus, Thr. Ir.
Gl. 138.6. ním romhúchat ním radhmillet nim indrisit
a rurcc a t. ┐ a n-amainsi (of temptation, etc.), ZCP vi 258.7.

egForm.p:
(tiachair) sorrowful: ba heinirt ocus ba diachrach
ro bás oicesium, SG 325.34. do bheir an t-iarthar diachrach
deorach, ITS iiia 118.2.

form.p:
[? ā, f.], tíachtu[n], tíachtain [gs. -ana]. Mid. Ir.
vn. of do-icc (see also tíchtu) cf. Sarauw, Irske Studier
§ 105. The vocalism is perhaps influenced by tíag- in forms
of téit, q.v.

eg.p:
I act of coming, reaching; taking place: iar tiachtain
Patraic, Corm. Y 883. fo-chen du t[h]iachtain ... a oighe,
637. cian rofeas do thíachtu sund, BDD² 359. atrogell
Édaín ... t. úaitsiu, Ériu xii 184.4. fath a tiachta an-Erinn,
Lec. 287a37 = fath a tiachtana, BB 43a35. bés ní tarissi iar
tíachtain, TBFr. 395. iar tiacht inmadha ... na hingine,
St. Ercuil 557. iar tiacht in lae, 1765. iar tiachtain doib
int shlebe (riachtain v.l.), TBC² 616. cia bad dóig diar
tiachtain, TBC 823. dlegar a tiachtain `it ought to be forth-
coming,' Laws i 128.6 Comm. cen tiachtain in marbtha
though death does not take place, 174.8 Comm. ? don ingin
ac ata in tiacht maicne, Laws ii 404.24 Comm. (but cf.
Stud. in E. Ir. Law 71 n. 1.).

form.p: II With prepositions.

eg.p:
(a) t. as act of escaping from:
na coimgend tiachtain as, Laws v 332.10 Comm.

(b) t.
de to be able: gan tiachtain de a tocuala, TTebe 3370.

(c) t. etar act of going between, ? interrupting: tiachtain
itir dilgud ┐ indechad, Laws i 14.2 Comm. ríge ... ocu do
gress, cen tiachtain eatarra
without interruption? (Plummer
MS. notes), Lism. L. 2102.

egForm.p:
(d) t. fo act of submitting to;
to be liable to; act of impugning: tiachtain fo dliged folt-
maisi to submit to, Laws v 122.11 Comm. tiachtain fo lan
in ecodnaig ann, ii 70.22 Comm. is coimgech in fine forru
im tiachtain fo coruib to impugn, v 130.10 Comm.

eg.p:
(e) t.
fri

(i) act of opposing: ar ba haigmeil leis a thiachtain fris
ima rigi, Lec. 269vb27. fonaiscid forro cen tiachtain fris
... co brath, RC xxiv 200.26.

(ii) act of submitting to: tiach-
tain ... re dliged
submitting to law, Laws ii 16.28 Comm.

(f) t. im: tiachtain ima reir
to abide by his decision, Laws
v 252.16 Comm.

(g) t. o: tiachtain o leith dire co trian
naithgena `is reduced,' iii 176.6 Comm.

egForm.p:
(h) t. tar act
of withdrawing from; mentioning; transgressing: dias
doroine cundrad ... is cuimgech cach fer dib 'masech tiach-
tain tairis, H. 5.15, 8a (O'Don. 1589). nocha chumaing ...
tiachtain tairis, H. 3.18, 642a (O'C. 1434). is imarcraid
n-imnisen tiachtain dar na nechib to mention, LU 7915. is
tíachtain tar breith senórach tíachtain tar do breith trans-
gressing, Ériu iv 134.21, 22. otchonnairc Dia tiachtain
doib tara thimna, Lec. 22vb43.

eg.p:
III In phrase ic tiachtain leigind engaged in learning,
later simply tiachtain: ic tiachtain leiginn ┐ proicepta,
Lism.L. 2613. saoi tiachtana leigind, FM ii 836.19. logh
a tiachtana no a oidechta, Laws v 212.21 Comm. calbh a
tiacht .i. cenn saoiechta, ZCP v 485 § 2 (B. na f.).

egForm.p:
ā, f. (< Lat. thēca) wallet, satchel (esp. for books): on
toga ... ar is taga set bis inti ... vel a tego, Corm. Y 1235.
dodosrat inna théig nuaig, SR 5868. cuirset na manaig
in cend ina téig libair, PH 925. atnagar in tiag libur isin
cuas, Trip. 556.9. dobertatar in téich cona reilcib isind
cuass, 84.17. do na bolgaibh nó do na tiachaibh leathair,
Keat. i 190.13. tiacha nach treabhair baoise, O'Bruad.
iii 4 § 2.

[o, m.] (tíag) little bag (cf. tíagánach and Dinneen,
O'R. s.v. tiachán.) ? To this: lethnaigi a tiagana gurab
comlethan fri seichid eilti, O'Dav. 231.

form.p:
o, m. (tíagán) one bearing a little bag: a thiaganaig,
Bruchst. i 32 § 74 = IT iii 103 § 198.

eg.p:
In cpd. tíamgestal `? feeble effort,' Met. Dinds. iii
260.15. Cf. tíamda.

egForm.p:
(a) slow, feeble: ní tiamdae tim som, Fél. Prol. 259.
admat na bi tíamdae weak, 294. tiamda .i. meata, O'Dav.
1571. tiamhdha .i. mall, O'Cl. geg rigda nar tiamda troid,
BB 61a46. nír gním tiamda téithmire, Met. Dinds. ii 66.14.
ria lotta nir thiamda tais, RC xlvii 290.11. cruaid lé ┐
tiamda a torrches, LL 49a33.

eg.p:
(b) obscure; (of persons) dullwitted: tiamda .i. dorcha,
O'Dav. 1571. duine tiamda techtas cruth | cen c[h]eill
glain dia ḟursundud, ZCP vi 267 § 8.

form.p: adv. later thíar. See also tíarain.

egForm.p:
(a) behind: cengal etaru tiar for a formna, Aen. 1064.
dairt i crand nairidi tiar, Críth Gabl. 224. meadh meanaidh
thiar ar a thóin, Ir. Review, 1912, 471 § 7. Referring to
previous passage in a book: cia nos labram tiar i stair,
Rawl. 69b10. don taoibh thiar `on the other side' FM v
1786.1.

(b) in the west, westerly: `cid dognither thiar innossa
... ?' `Tene do ḟatog ┐ bó derg do thelcud forsin n-áth
aniar,' Ériu iii 141.193. cont-ric fri Richis ... t. oc Lemain,
MU² 1029. d'éixibh Érenn thoir is t., ZCP viii 109.21. ni
dinsid tiar na tair, SR 7629. an taobh thiar, TSh. 173.
Referring to Ireland, in opposition to tair (q.v.): is imdha
toir laech leabhar ... imdha tiar toradh abhla, Reeves
Ad., 286.9, 13.

(tíar) crupper: gl. postilena, Ir. Gl. 265. cuir
uirthe a rí [bhus] rí ar neamh | tiarach do dhóchas daingean,
Aithd. D. 81.10.

act of seeking: atat fir Erenn agad lorgairecht ┐
agad tiaradh, TBC p. 185 n. 8. Cf. tiaradh `going' O'R.
Leg. agat íarraid.

(tíar) in the west: cleth Shligigh thiarain do thoit
| tigidh iaraidh a éroic, IGT Decl. ex. 681. cabhair Íle, a
earla nocht | tabhair thíarain do Thoigh Fhéilim, Sc. G.
St. iv 138 § 3.

[ā ],f. vn. of do-íarmórat. act of following,
pursuing: doróich in t. (sic leg.) forro co hÁth nImfuait
pursuit, LU 10463. bidh ann tiarmóracht dīāilgean `Ver-
folgung', Arch. iii 295 § 28. hi t. after: ícc co nindocbáil
inna tiarmoracht, Wb 30a26. air is gnáth lassar hi tiar-
moracht diad, Ml 40c1. is e in mac inti bís i tiarmórthecht,
RC xxvi 30 n. 8.

eg.p:
Gramm. postposition: ┐ .s. inna tiarmoracht, Sg. 16a14.
hi tiarmóracht són, 9a10. tiarmoracht `postposition,'
215a1. Of a noun governed by íar: iar fiur a thiarmoracht
`its progenitive,' Auraic. 1525.

egForm.p:
vn. of do-íarmórat; influenced by saigid,
see Ped. ii 600; succession, descendants: mani tancatar
tiarmoraigith cloindi, Laws iii 106.17 Comm.

o, m. (do-íarmórat) successor: isé aired ata
ní dona tiarmortachaiph, H.3.18, 244b (O'C. 462). cona
mbeth ina tiarmoirtecha[ib], H.3.18, 500 (O'C. 1244).
re ré na tiarmortach, H.3.17, col. 282 (O'Don. 371).

? As adj. succeeding, following: comarba na eclaisi tiar-
mórtighi, BColm. 104.27 (but Meyer emends to tiarmór-
tighthi and translates persecuted).

[ā, f.] (tíarmórtach) succession: ise i tiar-
mortacht iar tain, H.3.18, 500 (O'C. 1244).

i, m. (do-íarmórat) follower, successor, des-
cendant: giallu do tiarmortaid tar crich, Laws v 216.23;
218.35 Comm. a leth do thiarmorthaibh, 234.2 Comm. re
ré na tiarmorthuidh, H.3.17, col. 282 (O'Don. 371). Note
also: dona tiarmoirthibh, H.3.18, 500 (O'C. 1244). dona
tiarmoraibh, H.3.18, 423b (O'C. 984).

io,m. buttocks: le tóin 's le tiarpa, ZCP v 230. 1008.
cailleach an tiarpa, GJ vi 24.39.

o, m. (tíarpa) hip-sack: a dtiarpáin phutátaoi ar
tóin gach fir dhíobh, PCT 1294.

beginning: in Dei nomine, Amen. in tiasc
so, H.3.18, 358a (O'C. 756). in tiasca di fedaib, Auraic.
1760. in tiasca do bandialt, 5020. tiasc .i. tinnscna, ut
est, tiasc (sic leg.) ai i n-anmaim Dé, O'Dav. 1564 =tiasg
aoidh no uadh anmain Dé, Ériu xiii 38.1.

begins: Ollamh Fotla . . . | le[i]s cet (sic leg. MS.
cetna) -tiasco feis Temra
was first begun, Sitzb. 1919 v 92
§ 13 = ollamh Fodhla . . . leis cetna tiasgadh feis Teamhra,
O'R. s.v. tiasgadh. a nI Mainedh do tiascus . . . ┐ a mBoirinn
do forbus in `Toichid bratha' so (scribal note), H.3.18,
357 (O'C. 755).

eg.p:
is é rí Temra ca t. | is é in triath dá tic a lles, SG
385.20.

comla na tabair rem i tig Brocain mic Addi na t.
i mudu a nenbliadna berar do mac Aithchearda, BB 299b14.

beac a tiathugad (mark of a good horse), 23
P 3, fo. 20a (O'C. 1863).

egForm.p:
(=tuba ?) destruction: tiobha do róine in cloidhimh,
Duan. Finn i 49.13.

eg.p: see teipe.

form.p: ī (sometimes also ĭ-stem: fristib, Bruchst. i 67 § 154).

eg.p:
I t. (fri) touches, breaks against: conacca carraig mbic
frissi tibedh an tonn, RC x 88.2. ro thib tond tairis, CRR
34.21. doroicdis na tonna a dochum cu tibhtis uimme; no
thibheadh som frisna tonnuibh ┐ dobereadh a bhais fria
huan na tonn, Lism. L. 2171. Cuan Cruithne ris tib grian,
Ériu xi 197.12. Drobáis ristiben sál, LL 8b42. no stuag-
lubadh . . . in claidem sin . . . co tibead a inn re a urdurnd,
CCath. 5251.

II Through the phrase t. gen develops the meaning
laughs, smiles. See Vendryes, Études Celt. iii 42 ff.

egForm.p:
(a) t.
gen, gáire laughs, smiles; with fri, re smiles at: t. gen fris,
LU 3287. is mairg frisi tibi gen, 2977. cia rothibe findgāire,
ZCP vi 267 § 6. dremhan an caisgen tibhes, Fianaig. 16.12.
tibidsi gen gáire friu, BDD² 75. foglass a ngen (sic leg. MS.
ngein) tibes duit, Hail Brigit § 15. ni ro thib gen ngairi,
IT i 77.6.

(b) laughs; t. im laughs at; t. fri (re) smiles at, rejoices
at: t. cechtar de fria chéla, LU 5408. sech ní lungu ní thibiu,
IT i 79.52. t. dano in rí fochétoir, LL 282b22. tibis in
flaith re freagarthaib . . . in tuaiscertaigh, MR 158.7. ro
thib imma athair `laughed at,' Todd Nenn. 36 n. rotibset
im sodain, Ériu v 28.18. gon tibsid im sodain na Fomore,
RC xii 86 § 92. ro thib índ flaith . . . fri hAilill
rejoiced at,
Rawl. 84b13. tibis m'[fh]eoil is m'irrlabra | red berla suairc
solusta `were gladdened at,' Ériu viii 20.34.

eg.p: go t. toglaig Nathí | cinid fodlaig Ugaini, LL 22a29.
a maisse taisse tresse thibhraide, IT iii 96 § 151.
(cf. tibid).

(a) smile, laughter: tibri da leithe, Laws v 228.27 (.i.
gaire uime e do cach leth, 230.12 Comm.) tibhre seirce
smile of love', TD 13.8.

(b) ? shade, ? dimple: ceit[h]ri tibri ceachtar a dā grūad
.i. t. buidi ┐ t. ūaine . . ., TBC² 2033. tibri ániusa ceachtar
a dá gruad, BDD² 36. t. .i. finda na gruaide facbas in altan
dia hese, RC xvi 89 (whence Meyer derives meaning
hair;
but Windisch takes finda as abstract of find, TBC p. 168
n. 4.).

(c) laughing-stock, fool: ní ba th. dála, Tec. Corm. § 19.12.
t. cech mer, § 13.15. v.l. tibhre .i. amadán, O'Cl. ciar bo
thúi nirbo thibhri, LL 44b21. Cf. is eol dam fri tibri tra
| aided Libri is Broccada, Met. Dinds. ii 70.53.

egForm.p:
o, ā (tibre) laughing; dimpled: uas tuind tibrig,
LL 17b2. tonda tibreacha taebglana, TTebe 3532. tibhrigh
.i. gáireachtaigh. fri tuinn tibhrigh .i. fri tuinn gháireach-
taigh, O'Cl. gruaidh thibhreach, DDána 68.42. dá ghnúis
tibhrigh thonnghairthe, Studies 1918, 452 § 3. dá gruaidh
thibhrigh, Dánta Gr.² 63.14.

(cf. tobrúcht, tipra) outburst, eruption:
a thibhriucht na n-uli nuallach, PH 8238 = a thibrai na
n-uili dualach, YBL 162b28. Cf. inbert inbe cona t. |
d'inbib crú, Aisl. MC 81.7, 15.

o, ā (tibrecht) gushing, welling out: tipra
thibruchtach, RC xxvi 164 § 54. oc foluaimnigud ┐ ac
sugud int shrotha tibrechtaich teindtigi, TTebe 185.

gan t. re talmain
without touching
the ground,
MR 300.27.

eg.p:
Only in compd. tiburgér: cóica claideb (sic leg.)
fuilchrech tiburgéra `haarscharf,' RC xvi 89.13.

form.p: [io, iā] gl. Tiburtis, Sg. 57b4.

egForm.p:
u, m. (Cf. Eng. tick-tack) kind of board game: más tioc
dírech nó tioc cam, O'Gr. Cat. 579.33. air thioc, air ghea-
main, ar bhranaibh, no air thaipleisg mhóir, 23 B 18, 92.9.
saoir-bhearta an tioca (sic leg. MS. tiocha), 90.5. cluiche
teaca, L. Cl.A. Buidhe 131.33.

tiger: leogan ┐ t., matghamain ┐ dragun, St. Ercuil
1289.

eg.p: see tech.
see tíachair.

t. ona filedaib comad chucca tisad ar tus, LB
238cb49. Cf. téit IV 14 (b).

form.p:
n,f. vn. of do-icc. ns. a thíchtu, Wb 25b28. as. co
tíchtin, 25d1. tichtain, SR 3531. ds. íar tichte Crist, Wb
19b20. Later ns. often tíchtain. See also tíachtain.

eg.p:
Act of coming, coming to: in tain nád tomnibther a th.,
Wb 25b28. tíchtin inna epistle adrímisom ara thíchtin
fessin, 14d2. nirochreitset bas dia dícthin
to come to them,
Ml 90c22. ba mithig for t., Fél. Ep. 394. tichtu Patraic,
Lib. Hymn. 99.15. in setar lat . . . tichtu iarsinn luid isin
curach ?, Anecd. iv xv 1. dí bliadain . . . re tichtu Patraic,
Lat. Lives 2.12. iar tichtain duit asin linn, ZCP vii 307.1.
a mbeith ag tichtain for a cend, Arch. iii 309.6. feib dosfuc
. . . a tichtain buidig dia tig, SR 3531. atrugell . . . damsa . . .
ticht úaitsiu, LU 10901 = tiacht, Ériu xii 184.4. is focen . . .
do th., Ériu ii 222.5. mochen do th., TBC 1039. mochen
tíchtain degathar, SR 5988. nípu shirsan do fheraib Hérenn
ém tíchtain in tíri se, TBFr. 382. ic tichtain écsi dia
écsinib
teaching wisdom?, RC xxvi 12.9 v.l. (cf. tiachtain
III).

in oinchis t. (gl. Acts ix 25), Thes. i 497.2, see
725 and Ped. ii 491.

egForm.p:
m. IGT Decl. § 2 (39.20) pain ?: do sbairn sa tealaigh
a tigthe | maidhm ar chnedaib t. tug, IGT Decl. ex. 104.
ar nguin buinn, ar dt. tinn, DDána 79.29.
uncooked dough: t. .i. taos om, Corm. Y 401.

eg.p: see do-isca, tiscáil.

o tír t. dar nói tonnaib | don lir lethan, Todd
Nenn. 246.9 (LL 134b5).
see tuidecht.

tideal no barr blaithe lais, Laws ii 120.25 Comm.
Cf. titul.

egForm.p:
[ā, f.] (cf. fúapairt). attack, onset: otconnairc
tiduapairt na ngenti, Trip. 456.13. tucadh . . . tidhuabairt
echtrand . . . for ócaib in baile, CCath. 479. tidfhuabarta
na n-ammus gl. incursus, LB 67b51. na fhoelangtar . . .
ted[fh]úaparta, TTr.² 1710. do-rónsat tidfhuapairt Phetair,
PH 1782. go ttucsat tiughfhuabairt bhiodhbaidh orro,
FM iii 234.4.

eg.p: see tindnacol.

egForm.p:
triall ar.t., IT iii 75.14 v.l. dar t., 16. dar tídhle, 18.
tairgne tarathair a tidli, 77.22.

eg.p: see tindnacol.

form.p:
i Mid. Ir. denom. vbs. formed from
tidnacol, tidlacan, tidlacad. See do-indnaig and tindnacol.
o, ā (tidnaicid, tidlaicid).

eg.p:
(a) generous, plentiful: cona taoiseachaibh tenna tiodh-
láictheacha, BNnÉ 260 § 221. Tadhg Ua B., . . . tiodh-
naictheach séd ┐ maoine, FM iii 202.11. ben rathmar
ro-thioglacthach, Ériu v 74.11. fled buan-tigluicthech,
ZCP vi 71.19. fearthuinn tiodhlaictheach, Ps. lxviii 9.

(b) gifted, talented (?): tintodach tidnaictech amail
Cirine, Lism. L. 3321.
see taeb compds.

oiffrind lathaib techtaidib | iar t. cech claín, LB
261a81 = iar ndigdi cach cloein, Arch. iii 319 § 76.

egForm.p:
fair, seemly?: tuc ascaid togaide t., Met. Dinds. ii
60.5. fri toiche t., iii 118.103. cen túachli tich, 160.7. Cf.
2 tiug.

eg.p:
ata sruth usci tigban indsi na bīan, Ériu ii 114 § 40
= atá sruth uisci a tes teine a tracht innsi na pian, RC
xxiv 374.16. Leg. tig fán indsi.

egForm.p:
iā, f. (tiug) thickness, density: coica cubat tigi ammuir,
Rawl. 74b3. ocht dtroighthe 'n-a thighe ┐ dá throigh déag
d'airde ann, Keat. ii 6090. an lucht aga mbí cruas ┐ tighi
cuirp, Rosa Ang. 42.5. ar a luas ┐ ar a thigi asas, Auraic.
1322. re tighe na cethand, ML² 1717. le tighe an chumh-
gaigh `the tightness of the strait,' Ériu v 192.534. See tiget.

o, m. (tech, perh. influenced by tegdais; cf. .xl.
míle tighidhis, ZCP i 402.10.) house-keeping, husbandry,
provision, household goods: is maith a tigedus, IT iii 92.18.
bā t. cen mnāi, Aisl. MC 73.20. ar ngabāil trebe ┐ tigedhais,
ZCP xiii 166.8. tre febhus an tigedhais dorindetar, BCC
406.32. buaid tighidhís, Acall. 6659. beich . . . acc tionol
. . . a ttigedais, BNnÉ i 57 § 67. amhoil saithe beach ag
tiomarccadh a ttigheadhuis, Ériu iv 52.5. gur toirmisc
moran don tighedus ┐ co hairighe an cruithnecht `hus-
bandry,' AU iii 446.29. See tiges.

o, ā hospitable: fer . . . tighedhasach gan tathaoír,
FM v 1802.7.

eg.p: tonn trom tall tuaige tigheall, IT iii 87.2.

egForm.p:
fat: tuirc thenna th., Anecd. ii 59.3. Cf. tighean
`fat, gross,' O'R.

[ā, f.] tiger: amal th. nemnig, TTebe 642. amal tigir
tairpthig, 1578. mar da th., 4515. tangadar amach na
tigri, 2770. tigri trena tangnacha, Lism. L. 3650. etir
leoman ┐ mathgaman ┐ tigir, CCath. 3947. crocend tigri,
TTebe 2496. Cf. also: ticcri trena tuath-bertaigh, BNnÉ
99 § 10.

o, m. lord: cach mac tigirn, ZCP iii 214.5 (LU 9667).
Compd. bard poet of the fourth class, IT iii 5 § 1. tighearn-
bhard dō, duan ┐ forduan . . . a dhileas, 23.12. otha tigern-
bardd co ruicce driscona, Laws v 388.5.

eg.p: Cf. ócthigern.

form.p:
io,m. Later t and n. (Perhaps originally iā, f.,
sovereignty from tigern, with a development like that of
flaith. Cf. infra t. deisi, trír and gs. tigernae, AU i 198.6;
ds. thigerni, Wb 8d20, thigernai. IT i 190.5. v.l.) np. tiger-
nada, ZCP ii 4.3. tigernuidhi, Maund. § 148. gp. tigernad,
ZCP iv 43.3. dp. 'n-a tighearnadhaibh, DDána 89.4. ds.
on mbainnthiagernain, Ir. Texts iv 27.y. Also tigerna in
all cases except dp. tigernaib. IGT Decl. § 2 (39.21).

eg.p:
Lord, superior, chief: in tecttaire maith condaig indocbáil
dia thigerni, Wb 8d20. . . . Ailello tigernae ceniuil Fiachach,
AU i 198.6. tigerna Cremthinnae, Ir. Gl. p. 108.y. cach
rí ┐ cach tóisech ┐ cach t., TBC 5155. ic tairgnam da thigernu
dúthaig, MU² 134. o th. ┐ o mogaid, PH 4012. bad lugu do
chinaid fiadusom brath a `mágistrech' andás brath a `th.',
5166. for a ceile . . . for a tigarna, Laws v 164.20 Comm.
dithim gill a coimded .i. toitim gill a th., 378.4 , 14. t. deisi
gl. duumvir, Ir. Gl. 398. tigerne trír gl. triumvir, 399.

Of God: ro togaib a lamu suas docum a T., Laws i 6.9.
bai ferg aili la Día ṅdil | la th. do noebnim, SR 6841. i
n-ainm in t., PH 3737.

egForm.p:
Compds. ab lord-abbot: do thigerna-ab na mainistrech,
Fl. Earls 226.4. easpog lord-bishop: ro dearp don tigerna-
easpog, Fl. Earls 130.y.

o, ā (tigerna) lordly: ba tigernaig tuir throgaig,
Met. Dinds. iii 450.11. As n.pr. Auraic. 5794, RC xvii
420.12.

ā (tigerna) rules: ag so baramhail na n-úghdar
. . . dona críochaibh agus don nádúir thighearnas ina lucht
áitribh, Gadelica 6.7. an trath tigerndas coimplex fola
deirgi, Rosa Ang. 8.7.

[io, iā (tigerna) lordly: re linn trir tigearnaighi,
ALC ii 140.1. cuit t., AU ii 46.6.

g (tigerna) rules, dominates: tigernaidhi[dh]
do iascaibh in mara, BB 15b48. tigernaigit ┐ follamnaigit
do na cóic gradaib, PH 6242. lenaid na cuirp . . . gluasacht
na ndul tigearnuighes inntu, Mackinnon Cat. 38.33. gach
en ni a tigernaiginn an flice, ITS xiv 46.22. do mhnaib ┐
dferaib ana tigernaighind complex fliuch, Ériu x 147.10.
mar do thigearnuigh an pecadh chum báis, Rom. v 21.

i (tigerna) lordly: fa hé . . . an tres rí fa tighear-
namhla . . . do ríoghaibh Éirionn riamh, Keat. iii p. 381.15.

form.p: o and u, m. (tigerna).

eg.p:
(a) lordship, dominion, possession: tigernas an tire, ALC
i 344.9. do ghabhail tighearnusa Corcomodhruadh, FM
ii 618.1. ar tighernus an betha, ZCP xi 124.30. [a] beth
bliadain am thigernus, Fier. 171. ergi as a shudi thigernais,
PH 2641. tilach airechais ┐ tigernais Herend, LU 3439.
tulach tighearnais i tarrathar triar `metaph. of a man in
whose family the chieftainship has been for three generations'
(Plummer MS. notes), Laws iv 378.13 Comm. cf. ZCP xv
248.15.

(b) dues or territory of a chief: a uile chíos ┐ tighernus,
Fl. Earls 28.25. muc 's a ngníomh o sin amach | da
n-íocfaidh tighearnus ris an Sionnach, Misc. Arch. Soc.
i 190.8. do chuir a lán do tigernusaibh eile fa smacht,
ALC ii 306.24.

egForm.p:
(c) power, dominance: má bheir Dia do thiagharnus
damhsa | bheith slán ón láimh seo do leónadh, Hackett
xxvi 1. . . . bis tigernas ag lind ruadh, Rosa Ang. 4.17.
et as mar sin ata tigernas an da duil ele timcill a caili fein,
ITS xiv 14.19. do reir tigernduis adburdha . . . do reir
tiger[n]duis delbta = dominio materiali . . . dominio formali,
Rosa Ang. 88.12. an trat gabhas cail acu tigernas ar in
cail ele `prevails over,' ITS xiv 60.y. on craidi ata . . .
cathugud ┐ tigearnus ┐ fearg arrogance (?), Ériu ix 63.17.

o, ā (tigern) lordly: do tung dom Dia tigernmas,
Fianaig. 38.24. As subst.: ar treóin ┐ ar tóisig ┐ ar tigern-
mais, CRR 30. As n.pr.: T. mac Ollaig aird, LL 16b47.
T. tríath Temra thall, Met. Dinds. iv 20.26.

[o, m.] (tigerna) lord-ship, dominion: ni raibe
acht mí a tigerntus, ALC i 346.13. . . . fuasgailter ó thighern-
tas an diabhail . . . sinn, O'Hussey TC 97.16. tuc e fein
cona tigherntus fora cumus, St. Ercuil 1901.

[o, m.] (tech) householding, husbandry, household goods:
cin co roibh crodh no tighus ac duine, H. 3. 17, col. 560 (O'D.
781). doní tú tighes ar an ní atá ar láimh na fortuine, Mac
Aingil 61.15. a dtíoghas na féile, ZCP v 223.734. See also
tegdais, tigedas.

o, m. (tiges) housekeeper, entertainer: fer . . . dob
ferr do thighessach, ALC ii 282.24. do bhí C. ar na ríoghaibh
ba flaitheamhla do thigheasach . . . dá raibhe . . . i nÉirinn
riamh, Keat. ii 4740.

f. (tiug) thickness, density: ara teget immin cathraich,
Ml 48d14. ar thiget
on account of the thickness, Rawl. 74b6.
ba sí t. ind áirbaig, LU 6510. ordlach i t., Alex. 580. fri t.
na talmanna, SR 100. dia tigut, Laws ii 232.21. i n-a
tigit, 22 Comm. iter t. ┐ lethet, i 132.24 Comm. nac tairi
na da mer a t., Ériu xii 36 § 46 gl. 10. See also tige.

[u, m.] (tiget) thickness: do bhí leithead baise ar
thigheadas ann, 1 Kings vii 26.

eg.p: see tiugradus.

egForm.p:
[io, iā (tiger) tigerlike: rochuir a craicend tren
tigrigi, TTebe 4015.

eg.p: see tul.

form.p:
io,m. (< ON pili, cf. Bidrag 104). Later t and tiled,
o, m.

eg.p:
(a) board, plank: aithgin in ethair cona ramadaib ┐
cona sgulmaireda ┐ cona thilibh, 23 P 3, fo. 24c (O'C. 1919).
crithnugud clár ┐ taét ┐ tili, TTr. 1346. tairscur na tiled ica
timsugud, 1413. tuairc na tunna risna tiledaib, 1429.
suidhis an mílidh macáimh | ar an tileadh ndlúith nderidh,
IGT Decl. ex. 1836.

(b) stern: do bhí . . . ar an dtileadh 'na chodladh, Mark
iv 38. teileadh `stern,' Eg. Gl. 605. tileadh `stern'; seas
tilidh `stern-seat,' Arch. i 157.

(a) fills, occupies: tilidh a lán san bpár go ria an dá
bhruach, O'Bruad. ii 106.14. an mhéid go bhfuil an lea-
bharso ionar ndiaigh tilte do smior ealadhan, Ériu v 59 n. 2.
na sráid thilte thaoibhdhíllidh, v 58.100. an tír sin . . . baí
tilte techtaighthe acc Saxanchoibh, FM vi 2080.y. le rígh
Sacsan slóighthilte, O'Bruad. iii 68.20. mo mhionn sgine . . .
go bhfaidhinn dlúiththilte a ttéid, Studies 1923, 599 § 13.
Used with tí, clár, of filling the line or board (in a board
game): tilleit no teith (=tileadh na (d)títhe), Quiggin,
Poems from the Book of the Dean of Lismore, 63 § 7. a la
clarsi lane tilte (=a leathchlársa láintilte), § 8. Metaphori-
cally: iomdha ar neamh tí do tileadh, DDána 40.27. ar
gclár tilte, ar dtuir gan bhuing, 79.29. is clár tilte do thoi-
ghibh, Ériu v 60.105. Hence

egForm.p:
(b) controls, rules (often with clár, tí): do thil clár na
cruinne cé, Studies 1919, 73 § 8. Eriomhón an uair do thil
| clár Banbha ar bhél a shinnsir, L. Cl. A. Buidhe xxiii 9.
's nír léig déis na himreasna | tí ar feadh na tíre nar thil | 's
do geabh an ríghe ar éigin, 3 C 13, 743.13. tiltir Éire ó ghéis
Gáille, Aithd.D. 11.26. leat do tileadh teagh nimhe, Aithd.D.
68.15. tilid Éirinn gan ainimh | a héineing d'Inis Fhuinidh,
TD 10.11. Umhall an tráth fa dtilfe (sic leg. with MSS.),
RC xlix 171 § 19. grinn-bherta, as a ttilfe a thír | slighthe
is inlenta d' árd-rígh, GJ i 353.7. ? nár thíleadh dhí achd
fear faladh, DDána 40.27. Vn. tiled: fá ruire tilidh na
dtuath, DDána 93.16. a lámh thilte bhraonchláir Bhreagh,
TD 14.34.

form.p: u, m. vn. of tillid

eg.p:
(a) act of returning: mo thilledh is
truag dosan, O'Gr. Cat. 454.26. iar dtilleadh ó Mhaigh
Seanáir dó, Keat. ii 168.
(b) inflexion: en-t. uathaide, H.3.18, 88 (O'C. 155).

I Intrans. returns: do thilled assin tarais, BNnÉ
156.31. agus tillis sin an ditreibh, 157.13. mairg bus tinn
co ttille sin, ZCP ii 359.28. tillis go Guaire ris na scéalaibh
sin, Keat. iii 945. gidh fada dhó ar cuaird nach till, Hackett
iv 5. tillighidh tar [a] ais, Feis TC 179. tillis fria ┐ tuc
builli ina hucht dhí, 1758. till romad, Aisl. Tund. 143.3,

II Trans. turns, repulses, represses: till duinn na heich
┐ in carbad, ZCP viii 551.29. do-fhulaing tóir nach tilltir,
172 § 22. rún nach soithillte go síor, Studies 1933, 139 § 6.
go ttille an ghaothmhuir a geóin, 1921, 74 § 4. See fillid.

egForm.p:
i soft, yielding, pliant, feeble: timpan .i. tim (.i. bocc,
H.3.18) .i. sail, Corm. Y 1258. ní tiamdae tim som, Fél.
Prol. 259. `is tim sin, a Eochaid,' olsiat .i. `is sádail in
codlud a fuilidh,' Cóir Anm. 202. do thanaig thimm, Aisl.
MC 67.25. tond t. thana, Anec. i 63 § 117. do scían tím,
LU 3898. ni t. in gním, 4133. bad timm, bad docht tender,
Ériu iii 96 § 8. fúaratar bás, nar thimm techt (: mill),
Met. Dinds. iii 68.43. a gail co timm ro thaisig | co fil na
linn lánmaisig, iv 86.79. ni ba rochrúaid ní ba rothimm,
Tec. Corm. § 29.9. co nderna eocho trethi timmi ... dib,
CCath. 3136. ro bo truagh tím ... a comhradh, 3380.
aignedh t. `flaccid disposition,' O'Gr. Cat. 472.17. briathra
forránta, feidhm t., 556.17. más leor leat ar chuiris t.
have enfeebled, Dánta Gr.² 26.25. Compar. nirsa timmiu
innasin an t-imairecc, CCath. 2861. amail as time ┐ is
tlāit[h]i in ball sa quam alia membra, Corm. Y 149.

Compds. chride faint, tender heart: cach mac tigirn
timcraidi, ZCP iii 214.5. nirbo theidmnech timcride,
LL 131b37. a bhean an tiomachroidhe mhóir gentle heart,
Hackett xxiv 9. glún soft knee: an tiomghlún tearc,
Danta Gr.² 67.23. thríath cowardly chief: nir bo th.
troichnemail, LL 133a33. Dvandva compds: bog soft
and pliant: a bhairr thimbuig, O'Gr. Cat. 456.7. dil
tender and dear: stuagh thimdhil, Dánta Gr.² 67.38.
dímaín weak and idle: nach go tím-diomháoin do bhadar
an chuid oile d'árm an rí, Rel. Celt. ii 190.22.

m. (< Lat. thymum) thyme: ó t., gl. timo (=thymo), Sg.
54a18. tim, Rosa Ang. 258.23. boladh cúmhra an tíme,
Hard. i 208.3. ? Also tim: sgríobhtha a chert ar a
cheannas | i gcóig sélaibh slat thime | ar béalaibh mac
Moingfhinne, L. Cl. A. Buidhe 166.19.

vn. of *do-immacmaing (to-imm-ad-com-icc)
border, edge: sciath cobradach cona timacmac oir fair,
MR 64.2. See tacmang, timchomac, timchumang.

i,f. (? Orig. ā, f.; see táin.) vn. of do-immaig. timán
o, m. IGT Decl. § 35. timáin f. § 42. act of driving: oc
timmáin na mbó, TBFr. 425. thug Brian ┐ Cian ... an
mhaith sin leo ar chúlaibh ar thiomáin, Ériu i 80.15. ag
timain na muc, ZCP vi 276.13. timain penn so o Maeliosa,
H.3.18, 14b29 (O'C. 35). ré tiomantaibh diabhlaighthe
`by devilish impulses' (Plummer MS. notes), RC xxiii 24.4.

form.p: i (timáin)

eg.p:
(a) drives: ro thimain na .ix. n-uird
aingel, YBL 157a2. corro thionóil ocus cor thimáin iat
uile do dhruim degretha, SG 283.29. tiomáinfighthear a
ndorchadas íad, Isaiah viii 22. tiomāin !, Eg. Gl. 448.

(b) proceeds: do thiomáineadar dhéuntoil gu háit chruin-
nighthe an phobail, Acts xix 29. tiomáin air !, Luc. Fid.
274.16. tiomáin ort ! 278.12.
niss t. (sic leg.), Hy Maine 24.14 (Lec. 81va40).
see do-immoirg, timorcun and timarc.

egForm.p:
[o,ā] (timarcad) limiting, compressing: t'fherg
treith timaircthech, LU 3899. tinōl t. litrech nō guta
coherent, ZCP xii 295.2. coro lád snim tenn t., CCath. 668.

i, m. (do-immairg) corrector, chastiser: sencus
... a sen fil ann is oni is sensus, ciall; a cas fil ann is oni as
caistigatur (=castigator) .i. timairgthigh (=—thid) .i.
cialltimairgthigh gach raeda ina dlighedh, Laws i 36.1 Comm.

eg.p: see timna, timnaid.

egForm.p:
i, m. (timnaid) testator: dleaghair toil an tioman-
tóra do choimhlíonadh ar gach éinní, TSh. 5112.

form.p:
o, m., timarcad, timaircedu, m. Mid. Ir. vnn. of
timaircid.

eg.p:
(a) act of restraining, constraining: is all do
timurgud
to confine, ZCP iv 243.9 =is all do thimarcain
cach anma phíantair, LU 2448. a timmarcad fo reir na
ndáonnacht `it should be limited,' Mon. Tall. 152.14. fearr
iad so ná' seacht n-urdail | do shluagh thacair thiomar-
gaidh `a pressed army,' TD 2.38. ná gluaisidh trá dá
dtiomairg, Content. xxii 20. faill timaircthi
neglect of
restraining, Laws iii 384.16 Comm.

(b) gathering: líon a ttiomaircc ┐ a ttionóil, FM ii 1162.y.
teaglaim ┐ tiomargadh do dhaosgar-shluagh, TSh. 6649.
cuiris tiomargadh ┐ tionól ar maithibh Grécc co coitchenn,
Leb. Gab. i 80.16. See timorcun.
sceith re t. bais, H.4.22, 75a (O'C. 2101).

egForm.p:
Usually in phr. t. do it has been commanded
and originally 3 s. perf. pass. of do-immna, but later treated
as a noun; command: is ed t. ón athair nemda ... .i. tró-
caire, Ériu ii 194.5. timmarnad duit ó Ailill ocus Meidb
dul dia n-accaldaim, Aisl. Óeng. 11. t. duit techt lim-sa,
RC viii 60.26. t. duit iarom óm céliú, LU 3341 (SC). t.
duit ó Dia, Lat. Lives 39.9. timmarnad bethad ┐ imcomarc
slainte, CCath. 3297. tiomarnadh .i. aithne, O'Cl.

o, ā (timarnad) commanding (?): ic treb tuind
timarnadhaigh, IT iii 99.27.

eg.p: see 3 tim(m)e.

egForm.p:
vn. of *do-immaccai. act of looking at: ba lór
d'uathbas doib t. fair, CCath. 5331. See imcaisiu, tincisiu.

softness of heart ? : tiomchaire .i. tiomchroidhe no
maothchroidhe, O'Cl.

form.p:
o,n., later m. vn. of do-imchella. timchel, timchell,
tiomchal, tiomchall, IGT Decl. § 11; timchal, timchall,
§ 17.

egForm.p:
(a) act of going around, surrounding: it hé immefolngat
a thris timchel (sic leg.), Thes. ii 33.23. it trí mís deacc soli
oc timchull ærat tonimchéla luna inna óenmís, 19. iar
timchull (sic leg.), 22. grian a girando .i. o timchull, O'Mulc.
660. tréin iar timchul daire dall, SR 6355. greiss timchill do
denomh
surrounding movement, FM iii 632 9. gres timchill,
AU ii 524.10. beim timcill don erbull, St. Ercuil 1322.
cethernn timchill ríg Midhi `body-guard,' BColm. 102.2.
isinn aimsir timcill at that time (?), ZCP x 49.23. ar tí ar
dtimchill
attempting to surround us, Dán Dé xii 3. an chuairt
thimchil, DDána 26.5. nar ghabh iul timchil as teagh
`roundabout path,' PBocht 13.7.

(b) circuit, circumference, boundary: mochean dogní
timcheall tráth, SG 33.19. bói móin mór ... san athgoirit
roimhe aran slicchidh, ┐ timcheall mor aice, BNnÉ 208.21.
do-bir sí ... trí timchil, IGT Decl. ex. 514. atat ... secht
timchill im an talmain `sept zones' RC xxiv 372.33. coimh-
linas an firmamint a timcill, Ir. Astr. Tr. 62.13. t. .i. gabáil,
ut est, ma ro thimcill in filidh a áir `circulation' (Plummer
MS. notes), H.3.18, 654 (O'C. 1478) (cf. also tincell). ceithre
hordlaithe timcheall gach cloiche circumference, Flower Cat.
471.34. is daingean a timcheall
its boundary, ZCP iv 243.7=
is daingen a himtimchell na carcrach sin, LU 2447.

eg.p:
(a) t. around: doluid F. timcheall colléic co
mbaí isin Bruigh, Ériu xii 156.11. na co risat fir hErend
timchell, TBC 2890. co tainic t. o Loch Garman, RC xviii
51.25. in tromlonges t. i Connachtaib, CRR 58.y. téid-
leabhair tochailte tiomchol `engraved all round,' Studies
1923, 598 § 9.

(b) ar (íar) t. in succession, in turn: días fa sech ar tim-
cheall d'fianuip hĒrenn acum foraire, Fianaig. 56.26. a
gabail ar timcell dona daerceilib, Laws i 184.x Comm.
rígan ar th. díb, TTr. 441. co tiged gach drong ar dtim-
cheall, Études Celt. ii 298.6 = ar timchill, ZCP iii 35.7.
To this: gach lai timcheall, Lism. L. 2849. Cf. iar n-urd
timchill, 4163.

form.p: III ds. as prep. with gen.; later also i t.

eg.p:
(a) around:
timchull na Emna, TBC 1132. dobeired ... a mér timcholl
(hi timchul v.l.) lainne a scéith, Ériu iii 142.232. t. cacha
oenchrose, SR 372. cach ae dib t. aroili, BDD² 1339. ní
tugadh timcheall Áodha | a mílchoin ná a macáomha, IGT
Decl. ex. 930. d'eccla an tighe na timchall, Irish Texts ii
35 § 2. do iadsad Cenel Conaill uili a timchall in trenmiled,
Ann. Conn. 1401.26. i dtimcheall a dTighearna, Dán Dé
xiii 2.

(b) about, approximately: t. na Samna, Ann. Conn.
1404.4. timchiol mhedōin laoi, Fl. Earls 32.8. timcheall
is leath-uair sa ló, Donl. 474.17. timc[h]eal sē fichit éigin
ponta, Fl. Earls 86.y.

(c) (usually i t.) concerning, on account of, for the sake
of: an sciúrsadh tuc an t-aingel dó fen timcell Aedhain,
ZCP xi 128.7. a timcheall shubstainti na trī persan, xiii
181.1. amhail is mar dhéanfadh sibh im timcheallsa do
dhéanamh uime, Maguires of F. § 41. gach uile ainmían
dá raibe t. a gradha aice do dul ar cul uaithe, BCC 244.37.
Mac Donnchaidh ... do mharbhadh i mBreifne ... i timcell
fhuadáin creiche, FM vi 2048.17. do gab truaidhe mor
'na t. é, ZCP x 232.10. a dtimcheall luicht theagaisg an
tsoisgéil, Donl. 128.4. sa truaill atám 'na timcheall, `of
which I speak,' Dán Dé xx 42. do bhí taobh-nocht im
thimcheall
on my account, Ir. Monthly 1928, 331 § 8. cen
caithem t. a fine, Laws iii 50.12 Comm. ní faghtar troid na
t., O'Gr. Cat. 466.20. a arm timcell catha `his panoply of
battle,' CCath. 5203.

(d) besides, without, in the absence of: nidan chosmili
frisna preceptori atobsegatsi ar timchellni, Wb 14d37. ra
batar ... ingena imdai aice t. in lochta ra thurmisem, TTr.
718. a rád fria thimthirid inda timchol `by telling his servant
privately,' Mon. Tall. 146.32. issed atrubairt B. fri cach
ae t. araile, LU 8258 (FB). drubh 'na timcell .i. 'na ēgmuis,
ZCP v 487 § 15. cid mor do ernaigthi aile donemm t. na
paitri, PH 7987. fuit na bliadna t. in chorgais
apart from
Lent, 4979. timcheall na macraidhe .i. an égmais na mac-
raidhe, O'Cl. ? To this: mairc dos n-uc masu asa t., IT
ii2 176.64.

(e) In phrase i dt., in the ancestry of: gé bheith lá gan
réidhe riom | ar gcréine a-tá 'n-a thimchioll, DDána 5.16.
a mheic Máire nach muidh mionn | rogha Gaoidheal tá id
thimchioll, 102.44. an corp ar ar cheannchais neamh
| creidim ó táid 'n-a thimcheal, PBocht 14.37.
(f) With do-icc, etc.

(i) goes around: tic t. in luirg,
TTr. 404. tic timcheall in ech, Aen. 2848. tanic in brec
for t., Aisl. MC. 25.23.

egForm.p:
(ii) discusses: fada ata ag tocht na
thiomcholl `debating,' Studies 1919, 256 § 1. ata cás comairle
im chionn | fada as cóir techt na timchioll, O'Gr. Cat.
482.27.

eg.p:
(iii) circumvents: terc fer nach teguit timcheall,
Ériu iv 212 § 3. tecar na timchol
they are circumvented, Proc.
Brit. Acad. v 131 §23. tánic a ṅgáes t. Túathi Dé Danand,
MU² 2. nír édir theacht 'n-a timcheall, Aithd.D. 10.18.

egForm.p:
Compds. gerrad act of circumcising: circumcision:
an crodh e do thimchillghearradh, Donl. xvi 11. is tarbhach
an timcheallgherradh gu deimhin, Rom. ii 25. tesgad=
prec.: timchillteasgadh, TSh. 3290. trén strong all
around: ón torandchles timchilltréin tuc ... orra, Comp.
Con C. 106.19.

form.p: u, m. vn. of timchellaid.

egForm.p:
(a) act of going round, surrounding; circuit: ... torruma
sruithi ocus timchellad (sic leg. MS. timchelat) reilicc,
Ériu ii 228.6. do bhí sé ar dtimchelladh do choilltib móra,
SG 3.14. ic timchellad na trenfher, MR 238.6. ic timchellad
... a n-gruad, 184.24. ruibēr ro mhaith ag a timchiolladh,
Fl. Earls 72.9. ō 't—chualaid catha Cuinn do gach taob
'gā timc[h]eallad, ML² 323. ō tucais t. flatha for Fōdla
`royal circuit,' 1369. sinn ag innisin dhuit go dtáinic tim-
chealladh (sic leg.) do ratha `that the termination of your
prosperity has come,' MR 120.y.

eg.p:
(b) period of a fever: don lucht aga mbí aicses maille re
timchiollad =ii qui per circutum accessiones habent, 23 K 42,
11.3. isin cead timcheallud =per primos morbi circuitus,
238.17.
see do-imchella.

form.p: g (timchell).

eg.p:
(a) goes round: co timchollfuidhdís an doman, Maund.
155. corob airi sin timcillaiges in corp co huilidhi, RC xlix
5.16. nochan a tus timcillaighus an fiabrus amain, 23 P
10 ii, 12b55.

egForm.p:
(b) surrounds, encompasses, comprehends: frenes ainm
na sreabann noch timcillidhus an inchin, 23 P 10 ii, 28b34
do thimchiolluigh é fa ccúairt, 2 Chron. iv 3. Vn. timchel-
lugad: nach etir [Dia] do timchilliugud na do tacmong,
Mackinnon Cat. 23.29. ag timchiollughadh na fairge fa
ccúairt, 2 Chron. iv 3.

Vn. formation from *to-imm-com-icc-, girth,
circumference: t. i. timchell, ut est bo ... fiche dorn a t. .i.
ina timcell, O'Dav. 1495 = Laws ii 250.21. ocht nduirn
a t., ii 238.10. ogh rerchirce, .iiii. ordluighi a t., O'Dav. 1375.
Cf. .vii. nduirn a timcomat a bonai, Laws vi 497 n. See
timacmac and timchumang.

form.p: [ā, f.] (cuairt)

eg.p:
(a) circuit: timcheallad no tim-
chuairt, O'Dav. 1533. t. a thíre, 1534. tri tímchuaird
fiacal fota, LL 34b2 = tri nói sreth, Ériu iv 102 § 45. tucait
a trí timchuardda imman tech, MU² 871. tri timchúarta,
RC xxii 399.6.

egForm.p:
(b) In phrase i t., later t., as prep. followed by gen., around:
hi t. na scule se, Hy. 1.40. i t. firmiminte, SR 214. i t.
ind rigsossaid, 550. a ttiomchuairt an dunaidh sin, FDG
22 v.l. t. na sligedh, Fl. Earls 90.y. t. in tsēpēil, 124.x.

vn. of to-imm-com-icc-. circuit, girth: Eo
Mugna, mor in crann | tricha edh a thimcumang, Gwynn
Cat. 216.4 =tricha ed a himtacmang, Met. Dinds. iii 144.10.
See timchomac, timthacmang.

form.p: io, n. vn. of do-immdiben.

eg.p:
(a) act of cutting, hacking, mangling: cossa ┐ colla ... iar
n-a tímdibi dfaibhar a chlaidib, LL 406b15. hic timdibi
alale, St. Ercuil 317. dorat sé ... tescadh ┐ t. forra, 473.
ac t. na foghmorach, 610. tarlaicc an t-urchor sin dom
thimdhibhe, MR 286.15. dom thescadh, dom thimdhibhe,
ZCP xii 391.18. biasta fri t. anmann a n-ithfernd, Ériu ii
134 § 110. timdibhe .i. milleadh, O'Cl. Cf. icorisis .i. tim-
dhibhi, Arch. i 336 § 126.

(b) act of cutting short; killing: t. chodulta, Ir. Eccl.
Rec. xxviii (1910) 475 § 16. ropad t. saeguil ┐ flaithiusa
dó, Trip. 72.25. do seind in ceis ... do t. a saeguil, RC
xlviii 210.15. a saogal do t., SG 34.27. oc t. mo shaeguil,
77.28. nī cumaing duinēn anniū | mo shaégul do thim-
dibhiu, Éigse ii 109 § 5. bid t. dia sháegul for talmain, Ériu
ii 208 § 27. tánaicc timdíbhe saoghail an Iustis, FM vi
2256.14. re h-ucht troch do timdhibhe, MR 64.6. marbad
in tslóigh ┐ thimdíbe na tóisech, TTr.² 537. ic timdiba
(timdibi v.l.) thūath, KMMisc. 270.1. do b'éagnach uilc
thruim a timdhibhe, Aithd.D. 45.1.

(c) act of reducing; curtailing: t. flatha .i. eitirimdibe
uaidh ina flaithemnus, H.3.18, 243a (O'C. 456). t. .i.
dibhail a dhligi dhe, 247a (O'C. 472). t. aneich dleghar ann,
Laws iv 252.8 Comm. cét cech míl cen t., Met. Dinds. ii 2.7.
a cethair fichet as glé | agus naoi ccéd cen timdhibhe, FM
ii 614.4. timdhibhe .i. laghdhughadh, O'Cl. Cf. 3 tim(m)e.

egForm.p:
o, ā (timdibe) destructive: tres t. Muigi Treg,
Fen. 378.25.

eg.p: Cf. deoch timdibigh, ZCP iv 468 § 11.
see do-immdiben.

egForm.p:
iā, f. (cf. W. twym) heat: ni léicc a chorp hi timmi
.i. i topliuin .i. in teas, Hy. 2.32. lace ┐ ladg .i. a lacte .i.
ō ass ar a time, O'Mulc. 775.

iā, f. (tim) fear: ferr teinni na timmi, TBC 3280.
nír[ó] léicc cruas craidhe dó time do dénam, CCath. 2066.
eochair timme teched, ZCP vi 270 § 8. creach gan tóir
time [na] taoibh, A. Ó Dálaigh iii 4. tláithe ┐ time a fhogh-
namha, FM vi 2142.22. ní ar time dodhechaid, ZCP i 364.z.
airm i tathaim ar thimme | Clíach rochachain ceólbinde,
Met. Dinds. iii 224.17. ni ar thime ná ar tlás, FM iii 518.7.
ni ar teithed na ar timme, Ann. Conn. 1318.3. ar thime
ocus ar theichthige, MR 314.19. cen t. fearless, unyielding:
Mac De Athar cen timme, SR 8274. do réir riaglai cen
time, Fél. 166.26. do righ Temhrach gan time | do innis
a h-aislinge, SG 68.41.

io, n. vn. of *do-imben. act of curtailing: dlighidh
a saerbiathadh fo lin cen timbe (sic leg. with MS., Plummer
MS. notes), Laws iv 344.23. time saoghail d'imirt air, Oss.
iii 92.27. cach crand cen timme ria thúr `without exception,'
Met. Dinds. ii 58.8. rosmarb cen timme na teist, iv 338.3.

form.p: io, n. vn. of do-immgair.

eg.p:
(a) act of asking, requesting: `tiomghoire' iarruidh, Met.
Gl. 24 § 19. iar na th. fri hail | d'ingaire caire Labain, SR
2967. co mbai forsin dergud occaisseom oc a th., Anecd.
i 10.10. tláithe t., Tec. Corm. § 16.73. ba menic didu a t.,
RC xxv 20.9. ba talchar in t., xxxvii 348 § 57.

(b) act of summoning: tánic timgairi dó tíchtain día
crích, LU 10346. fer na fil im ḟiadnaise | im triamainse
t., Met. Dinds. iv 322.37.

(c) in Laws, act of demanding back (of loans, etc.): ce
be uair dib do nethar a t. ised dlegair a naisic, Laws iii
492.19 Comm. ni misech fer in iarraith a thiumgaire, ii
170.z. cethri timgairi dorímesuim, ii 164.3 Comm. mad t.
cen tathchur, 8 Comm. facaib in flaith trian ar tiumgairi,
ii 206.18 Comm.
see do-immgair.
see tingell, tingellad.

form.p:
g (tim) softens, mitigates: no timmiginn gl.
mitigare, Ml 70c4.

g (cf. 1 timme) sweats (?), grows warm (?):
sudo sudor allas, madeo [leg. caleo, Edd.] timmigim, Thes.
ii 42.17.

egForm.p:
m. (tim) coward, weakling: Eochaid T. ...
is tim sin, a Eochaid ... conad desin ro lil Eochaid T.
de, Cóir Anm. 202. Eocho Timmín ... conid de sin ro len
timmín de, LL 315a41, 46 (SG ii 493.45, 49).

form.p:
io, n. vn. of do-immna. ns. a timne, Wb 3c33. ds.
iar timnu, 6d2. np. timnae, Ml 71b14. gp. timnae, 46c24.
timpne, Wb 4d24. dp. iar timnaib, SR 3138. Later m.
and f.: a haithle na timnai, TTebe 3843. is é mo thimna,
RC xiii 460 § 60. Also t: na timnadu, PH 7952, timnadai,
5922, but usually indecl. in Mid. and Mod. Ir. gs. tiomanta,
TSh. 5162 (on analogy of part.).

egForm.p:
I act of commanding, command, precept: timna .i. aithne,
O'Dav. 1566. comallaid a timnae ┐ gnímu, Ml 115c2. iar
timnaib na mbrátharse, SR 3062. ná rochomaill a thoil
┐ a thimna, LU 2342. iar timnaib ind rígsa, Fél. Prol. 27.
céne connoither mo thimnasa, Mon. Tall. 129.31. is dia
sheirc conairliter | a thol ocus a thimnae, Ériu i 195.2. do
thímnaib na sruithi, 196.9. deich timna Dé, BColm. 100.7.
na deich timna, Hib. Min. 1.21. na huile timna, Laws i
114.z. tiomna Críost níor chomhuill siad, DDána 31.7.
In phrases tar t. against the commandment of, techt tar t.
to transgress the commandment of: rofitir in Coimdiu no
regad duine dar a timna asbreth fris, Ériu ii 108 § 25. dar
t. a tigernai, SR 1162. techt dar t. in rig, LU 4066. tóeb
do thabairt riu is dar timna, PRIA xix C 542 § 10. is tearc
tharrla | díobh gan teacht tar tiomna, Dán Dé xii 2. an
chliar tar tiomna ag tuitim i dtréatúireacht, O'Bruad. ii 4.4.

eg.p:
II act of recommending; sending off: do bí aga thiomna
do Dhía, Misc. Hag. Hib. 103 y. broimm crúaid iar n-ithi
arba | i timnu anma Concluchair `speeding the soul,' RC
xiv 191.20. Cf. fri timna bais `at the point of death,' Ériu
v 120.24.

(a) act of bequeathing; will, testament: ag t. ferainn
dia macaib, IT iii 372.3. íarna th. dó, ZCP viii 328.21.
mad ail leis ni do t., Laws iii 52.1 Comm. dorigni t. dia
rigi ┐ da ferann, RC xxvi 132.2. is é mo th. cen on | atbiur
ingra do Mac Con, RC xiii 460 § 60. tiumna fri hec, Laws
v 368.3. do réir tiomna do órdaigh, BNnÉ 262.2. atbáth
gan tiomna gan aithrighe, FM ii 1182.7. fāgbuis a tt. thol-
tanach an crann pailme ... ag H. a n-oighrecht, Fl. Earls
230.2. éisd rem thiomna, a Thighearna, DDána 62.13.

(b) bequest, gift: timna in rig, RC xviii 182.5. do chuid
tiomna
as a bequest, PBocht 9.29. beir lat ... in cilfing
mbicc-sea do timmna `as a keepsake,' Mer. Uil. 167.

(c) act of disposing of, allocating (?), disposition: munar
leis í ré tiomna, Content. vi § 108. tiomna Iughoine ar
Éirinn, iv § 47. tiomna Colmáin ar a cheird, Studies 1918,
99 § 9. clár tiomna na trócaire, DDána 21a.12. Cf. ó bhias
liom lá na tiomna | maor tobhaigh an tighiorna
day of
judgment, DDána 11.7.

(d) Testament (of Scriptures): mar dobí sa tsentimna,
Maund. § 10. mhfuilsi na tiomna núaidhe, Matt. xxvi 28.

(e) bargain, covenant: dobhēr dhuitsi ... tearc tiomna
is daoire dhuit, | maoine iomdha 'na éiruic, ZCP xii 381.3.
tiomna nār dhual do dhemhan | do thuar diomdha an
Dūileamhan, 30.

Note also: áit a mbia mo thaisi, mo thiomna ┐ mo thir-
uairsi `remains, corpse' (Plummer MS. notes), BNnÉ i 266.21.
see do-immna.

form.p: g (timne)

eg.p:
(a) orders, commands: tiumnaigther
uad co tuaith, Laws i 136.1 Comm.

(b) commends, entrusts: tiomnuighim dhuit mo smuain-
tighe, Donl. 260.6. tiomnuighidh an bocht é féin duit,
Ps. x 14.
see tinmed.

dobreth rátha na n-uile dúla ... do t. rig
Caisil dia shil dogress, Irish Texts i 20 § 9. Leg. im ollamnas.

egForm.p:
(? omun) act of terrifying ? : bid ann t. a ndūine,
Arch. iii 295 § 25.

form.p: ā, f. vn. of do-immoirg. Later timarcain.

eg.p:
I act of shortening: a thimmorcuin `its shortening'
(correptio), Sg. 18b3. ius inna timmoircne, 221b8.

(a) act of restraining, repression, discipline: i tim-
maircnib gl. in carceribus, Wb 15d31. is do dlegar ... a
cosc ┐ a timorcun fri hurdu ecclaisi, LB 12a35. fria tinchosc,
fria timmarcain, SR 4548. timargain sula .i. gan sír dhechain
neich do chléirech ach a liubhar (sic leg.), O'Don. Suppl. s.v.
tiomargain. tri timorgain cuibsi no gnuisi, H.3.18, 9b (O'C.
21). brīathar āilgen, timarcain borrfaidh, ZCP iii 27.3. crō
timorgne, xii 364.7. timargna fri ōentrātha, iii 25.14.
mac son bīs i tesgaire a athar ina timaircnib techtaib,
xiii 23.17. do timorgain in fuilt sin immo cend `to confine,'
CCath. 4120.

(b) act of forcing, compelling: inna timmaircnea gl.
coartationes, Ml 55d18. is do tra dugnither insin dia chosc
┐ timmarcuin dochum dáe, 111c3. fri timarcain cáich fo
recht, SR 7097. forfhemdinn a thimargain, 1338. da
noemog rohidhbratar inn-oighe do Dia a rop ail leisseom
a timarcain fri feraib, Anec. iii 40.6. timorcain dligid deit
for fer, Laws v 478.23 Comm. dia timorgain do reir, Mann.
and Cust. iii 491.19.

(c) act of driving (cattle, etc.): oc timmargain a cethra do
etrud, LL 167b20. tiomargain cethra no cruidh, BNnÉ
263.5. timargain dam fri a ngabail, Laws v 486.23.

(d) act of gathering, collecting: forcraid cech baill do
thinól ┐ do thimarcain ind féin, LU 2584. ic tinol ic timar-
cain na scel nuathmar, BB 257b50. in comhlín sin do
cinedhaibh ┐ do ríghaib do timorcon d'énrí[g], CCath. 1613.
airecht do timurcain, Laws i 202.11 Comm. ag tiomargan
a lebhar, SG 2.12. cian ataoi ag tiomargan cean, A. Ó
Dálaigh xl 3.

(e) act of levying: etir saigid ┐ timmarcain, Cáin Ad.
§ 30. timargain érca ar in flaith, H. 3.17, col. 419 (O'Don.
516). dlegar do na flathaib timorgan caich dib for a fearann,
Laws iii 20.8 Comm.

form.p: io, iā part. of do-immoirg.

eg.p:
(a) shortened, short: cid timmartae péneuilt, Sg. 52a15.
in tan is timmortae, Corm. Y 114. cach timarta ar chena,
Auraic. 1550.

form.p:
(b) straitened, strict: timmartaib gl. artís, Ml 27a4.
timmartae gl. arcta, 44a2. Cf. dedairn.

eg.p:
(a) restrained, punished: timmartai gl. cohibetos,
Ml 121d5. amal a[ta] timmartai gl. castigati sint, 118d13.
síl nAdaim at timmarta, SR 8131.

(b) constrained: nephthimmorti fri slond n-intliuchta
not constrained to express a meaning, Sg. 3a8.
Compar. ata thimmartu gl. artiores, Ml 57a6.

dobeir tra timmorlai ┐ immetlai menman, IT
ii2 107.23 = dobeir tra etir eri ┐ etlai ┐ todiuri menman,
Alex. 1077.

egForm.p:
(a) act of killing: death: atait secht timortana
... .i. t. in fir tuites isin cath ..., Laws v 236.16, 18 Comm.

eg.p:
(b) dead stock, chattels: cro .i. na beodile ┐ timartain .i.
na mairbdile, H.3.18, 151, half-leaf 9 (O'C. 270). ag agra
arin tiumartain riasiu tí aimsir tobaigh for biu, Eg. 88, fo.
39 (40)c (O'C. 2487).

egForm.p:
o, m. player on the `timpán': cúisig, timpaig cen
triamna | filid ocus faen-chlíara, Met. Dinds. iii 18 235.
Cf. timpánach.

form.p:
o, m. (< Lat. tympanum). Also occas. f.: umae
bīs inti, Corm. Y 1258. IGT Decl. § 35.

eg.p:
(a) timbrel, drum: siur do Moisi, Maire már | iar sain ro
sephainn t., SR 4042. Muire ... ┐ si oc senmaimm thímpain,
LB 118b44. ghlac sí tiompán na láimh, Ex. xv 20. bidh
foghur and mar guth timpáin, mar toirrnigh, Rosa Ang.
26.20. da fogruidhi an medhon re bualad mar t., no mar
tabur, 268.14.

(b) some kind of stringed instrument: ic seinm a thimpáin
téidbind, SR 6060. timpān .i. tim .i. sail ┐ bān .i. umae
bīs inti, Corm. Y 1258. cruit .i. ar timpan sin, Laws v
106.34 Comm. timpan bec ro bói ac na mnaib | cona leth-
rind airgid báin | cona deilgnib oir buidhe | cona thétaib
findruine, Acall. 5610. timpan aircit ana laimh | fa hor
dearg teta an timpain, 362 n. fer becc, trí thét ina t., RC
xiii 438.1. tri téad is laige táin | do chím a lar do thiompáin,
Rel. Celt. ii 293.14. timpan becc ... ┐ in sepainfidhtir duit-si
he? ... atnaigh-sium a mher tharse, RC vi 183.13. re foscad
... na t. 'ga tadall d'aigthib ocus dformnadaib eand ocus
ingen na suad 'gá sarsheinm, MR 168.x. tolg do thetaib
timpain, Laws v 276.5 Comm. orgána et timpána et cláir-
siocha, Aisl. Tund. 114.6 = orgáin ┐ timpáin ┐ cláirseóir
ag a seinm, 139.11. timpan creda in lāim chli in gilla,
Anecd. i 2.21. imirt sgéith Lagha ar do láimh | ar chléith
tana do thimpáin, IGT Decl. ex. 882. muna mbeith an
dán | ag cruit téidbhinn ná ag tiompán, DDána 72.29.

egForm.p:
o, ā (timpán) like a `timpán': a chruit tiom-
pánach théidbhinn, Dánta Gr.² 16.116.

As subst. o, m. player on the timpán: timpanach gl.
timpanista, Ir. Gl. 6. arsentis crutire ┐ timpanaig, LU
10134. mac in timpānaig na tét, Ériu ix 49 § 31. ni fes co
tanicc na co ticcfa choidchi a commaith do timpanach,
Ann. Conn. 1328.12. sai timpanaig, 1364.10.

[ā, f.] (timpán) art of playing the timpán: ollamh
timpanachta, Tromd. Guaire 969. timpanacht ┐ cruiti-
reacht, Aen. 1420. ollam Tuadmuman re timpanacht,
AU ii 510.18.

(< Lat. tympanites) dry dropsy: ┐ co hairighi
t., Rosa Ang. 268.8. co leighister t. da [ti] fiabras na diaigh,
282.4.

(< Engl. temper) Med. act of moistening:
pudar do ghenamh dhi ┐ a thiomprail le sugh clamhain,
23 K 42, 336.22. becan dairget beo arna timperail le seili
duine, Irish Texts v 84.6. indus go mbiadh an biadh arna
comusg ocus arna timprail, Reg. San. 20.31.

(< Fr. tempeste) accident, misfortune: bhain tiom-
puiste dhom, Arch. i 157.27. See tubaiste.

[o,ā] (timpiste) accidental, unfortunate: Cormac
mac Domhnaill ... do marbadh go timpeisdech, ALC ii
200.8. Tadg ... O Dubhda do tuitim do bharr caislein ...
occus a marbhadh go timpeisdeach, 432.17.

form.p:
g (perhaps from *do-immsaig, but no deutero-
tonic forms are attested and it is treated as a simple verb).

egForm.p:
(a) brings together, collects: Lug ... rostog is rostimsaig,
Met. Dinds. iii 218.44. in bo cusani timsaigther le do
biadaib aile, Laws v 434.8 Comm. ratecrad ┐ ratimsaiged ┐
ratimmairged trelam in tromlestair sin, TTr. 122. timsaigid
a shluaig leis, TTebe 1441. ra timsaigit ┐ ra timmairgit
fir hErend lé-si, TBC 6121. do thimsaig ┐ do tinoil an cuid
do bi spreite, BCC 6.13. Hence collects one's thoughts, draws
a conclusion: tiomsuigheadh se ionn a choimhne
let him
sum up, Donl. 320.z. tar éis gur thiomsuighis do pheacaidhe,
288.3. as na raitibh sin timsaigter
it is gathered, understood,
Ir. Astr. Tr. 16.5.

eg.p:
(b) compresses, squeezes: hi tul a scéith chimsaig cóim
| ro thimsaig, tuc in maccóim, Met. Dinds. iii 128.13. coro
timsaig ┐ coro thimairg Ageleius ┐ co rotrascair dochum
lair, TTebe 2565. in mac beg timsighthar a lighi cro, 23 Q 6,
45b (O'C. 1818). an dara feacht do thiomsuigh an gcriaidh
gcéadna, TSh. 316.

(c) compels: nis timsaich greim riaglad do beith gan
ni, Mon. Tall. 145.5.

II comes together, assembles: tionoilit tra ┐ tiomsaigit
as gach aird arabhatar, BNnÉ 273.12. ra thimsaigsead na
Tiabanda uile co haeninad, TTebe 4289. ro thimsaigeadar
sluaig in domain, CF 4. timsaighit a ghaelta ┐ a charait
chuige, Marco P. 164. do t[h]iomsidur seacht ccatha na
gnāthfēine cum an tsīodha, Feis TC 1263. as i naduir an
aeir .. in tan fuaras, timsaighi dinnsaigi a celi
it presses
together, Ir. Astr. Tr. 54.8.

form.p: Vn. timsugad, q.v.

egForm.p:
io, iā part. of timsaigid gathered together: ina
trebaib ... timsaichti, LB 123b34.

o, ā (timsaigid) concentrated, collected? : is
combruth coteigthi ┐ is tégud timmsaigthech, TTr. 1510.
rucsat trethan trén t., 1677. do thunidi thimsaigthech,
1678.

close, ending: nirbo thréis in t., Met. Dinds.
iii 438.20. ? Leg. int imscarad.

eg.p:
rapa th. tecair thinnenais, TTr. 1735. ? Leg.
timsugud.

form.p: u, m. vn. of timsaigid.

eg.p:
(a) act of bringing together, collecting: abair re Bran
Tuatha De Dhanann do thimsachad d'ar cabhair, CF 225.
robui 'cu timchellad ┐ 'ga timsugud, TTebe 3511. maille
re cioscháin Laighen ... do toccbáil ┐ do thiomsucchad,
BNnÉ 264.12. rocuir tinōl ┐ tiumsugudh ara muindter as
gach aird ina rabudur, ZCP vi 40.25. trascras cach t. bís
ar a chind, TTr. 1982. saor a-bhos bláth na faighthe | a-nos
tráth a thiomsaighthe, DDána 7.6. lá tiomsuighthe na
dtrí sluagh, A. Ó Dálaigh, xliv 11. ní chéala cách | a sgéala
i dtráth an tiomsaighthe, PBocht 6.10

(b) act of compelling: aca timsugud fo luigi cana, Laws
v 236.21 Comm.

form.p: o (in pl. generally s), n. Cf. étach.

eg.p:
(a) covering, garment, cloak: timtach fir is gnath a ndail,
Laws v 238.19. cona timthaigib dergóir, SR 6278. an
romba dech do thimthagaib flatha fer nGaoidel, Corm. Y
1059 (91.6). i n-a thimthuch trénmíled, TTr. 1035. timm-
thaige ┐ erredai ┐ étaige, 596. tucusa cor ┐ coibchi duit ...
.i. t. da fher déc d'étach, TBC 44. eter lín ┐ chostud ┐
timthaige, 5204. sech a t. sechtair, 211. a thimthag
ōenaig, ZCP viii 310.28. issé mo th. robói im Chrimthan
| i cath Oche, MS. Mat. 488.15. bretnass gelairgit i timthach
in bruit, RC xxiv 200.4. do rad Muiredhach tuarastal dó
.i. céad bó ... agus a thimtheach budhéin, L. Cl. A. Buidhe
12.8. sciath cobradach cona th. oir fair (timtacmang,
tiomacmach v.ll.), FDG 578.

(b) accessories, complement: bō cona timtach, Laws v
432.18 = ZCP xiv 361 § 19. cona t. di saill no charna, i
48.3 Comm. dartaid inidi cona timtach, iv 306.3 Comm.
loracc cona timthucc, Trip. 120.22.

? coniscumhaing mu Rīg rān | mu beith ic timtach cin
tār, ZCP vi 260.17. ? co timtach fri marbu, ii 315.14.

egForm.p:
(a) covering, garment, cloak: t. dá fher dēac,
TBC² 1104. cēt snāthēicne do c[h]arrmocal c[h]umascda
i timt[h]acht fria chend
as covering, 2033. t. da fer déc
d'etgud cacha datha, TBC 3027. fuan ... ina th. `als seine
Kleidung,' 5552. itir timtacht agus eccasg, 5463. t. dá
tricat do trēnferaib, Celt. Rev. i 220.11. in fer ga mbí t.
rig, FDG 305. intan gabus ime a t., Anecd. i 48 § 12. co
timtachtaibh anetargnaidea do side ┐ seric, Aisl. Tund.
112.20. cona thimtacht óenaig, LU 10192. corn lámha
rígh cona th. do ór derg covering, ornament, Lism. L. 2982.
is do thimthachtuib a bhfiadmil doniad eirreda hides,
Marco P. 103. doniat erreda ... do croicnibh ┐ timthach-
tuib a bhfidhbhuidi bark, 121.

eg.p:
(b) girth, circumference (cf. timthacmang): fidh ... .v.
mílí déc ina timthocht
in circumference, Marco P. 49.
atconnuic Marcus ... in dishoillsi sin 'na timthocht
around
him, 10.

(<*to-imm-to-ad-com-icc-, cf. imthacmang,
tacmang).

(a) act of surrounding: go raibhe an mádh
áluinn iar n-a thiomthacfang d'fhearann aggarbh, Desi-
d. p. 14 n.

(b) girth, circumference: Eo Mughna, ba mar in crann |
tricha edh a th., Fél 258.21 = timcumang, Gwynn Cat.
216.4 = himtacmang, Met. Dinds. iii 144.10. beim ... ina
th. ar medon, St. Ercuil 1323. .lx. míle cémenn ina t.,
CCath. 18.

(c) dress, equipment: tiomthacmung tigerna, eter each
┐ erredh, Misc. Hag. Hib. 44.6.
See timchomac, timchumang.

egForm.p:
(cf. immthairec, tairecc) preparation: ro
seinntea stuic leo fri tímtharig longthi, Alex. 704.

[u, m.] vn. of do-imthas. act of checking, restrain-
ing: a timtasad for caulae `they must be checked and re-
called,' Mon. Tall. 151.16.

io, iā part. of do-imthas. compressed, straitened,
narrow: timmthastaib no cumcaib gl. fixis labris, Sg. 6a17.
cona thengaid do métail ... timmthasta, Aisl. MC 89.25.
sētigi in tige āiged ocus sē timmthasta timmaircthi `rolled,'
11.18. is cumang ┐ is timtasta in sed gl. arcta via, LB
36a39 (PH 4004).

eg.p:
dēna ingeilt ois | narbat t. (imterc, v.l.) tais,
KMMisc. 262.1.

egForm.p:
o, m. (orig. n. ?) circumference, border: .l.
cathscíath n-airgdide cona timtimchiull d'or, TFerbe 27.
See timchell.

[io,]m. servant: mad ad timtire umal do Dia, D
iv 2, 74 va2. fri timthirib na hidparta, CCath. 960. Cf.
timthirthid.

o, ā (timthire) attendant: Ronan diadha degtim-
pirech `assiduous,' Misc. Hag. Hib. 124.27. As subst.,
servant: ainm in timthirig-sin, PH 1002. fria a timtire-
chaib écraibdechu, 3878. timthirigh na righna, St. Ercuil
104.

form.p: ā, f. vn. of *do-imthiret. Later timpirecht.

eg.p:
(a) act of going to and fro: cumma ┐ t. bech i llau ánli
cach hae sech alaili súas, BDD² 1169. t. na n-aingiul imon
tir angelos circumvolitantes, Lat. Lives 102.4. t. n-aingel
issin mónai dond lige, KMMisc. 212.18. t. angel dond ligi
dochum nimi, 214.2. do t. iter Dia ┐ doinib, PH 6228.
co faca t. na n-aingel súas ┐ anúas and, LU 9825.

egForm.p:
(b) act of serving, ministering to; ministration: bieid
crich for timtherecht cacha dúlo, Wb 13b28. inna timth-
rechta ind labrada gl. officia, Ml 42c4. in ointimthrecht on
frinni, 53b20. timthrecht deggnima du edbairt dait, 73a10.
atrebat ní tria timdirecht, Sg. 35a2. oc t. in tslóig uile,
BDD² 1307. dorat sē laithi ... don domnach da th., Ériu
iii 143 § 4. oc a t. na sruithi sin, Mon. Tall. 136.25. t. inna
pīan `ministration of torments,' Ériu ii § 120. consacratar
inna huili grada-sa frisna timtherechta cetna iar pennuid,
vii 142.14. is díaisneisi ... a thimthirecta inna dhūlib ō
tosach domuin, ii 140 § 151. gid urd ... aon oidchi den
timtirecht, Laws i 22.24 Comm. na dernasamar t. ┐ umallóit
duit, RC iv 248 § 10. umalóit ┐ t. do'n fhoirind beit hi
carcair, PH 6002. dar trealmaib timtirechtai a anala
`through the gear that served his breath,' CCath. 4701. aingil
nimhe do bheith ag timpireacht dó, TSh. 3429. Of religious
ceremonies: ithé són leviti olchene nobítis oc t. inna nidbart,
Wb 10d17. eolus timthirechta a graid, Ériu i 218 § 2. t.
imāin is leis | lasin fer grāidh, RC xxxvii 346 § 15. lestra
imda oir ... do th. (sic leg.) altore De, Anecd. iii 75.27.

eg.p:
(c) act of supplying: co [a] timtireacht a triur | do
biudh (muntere) nime, Snedgus u. Mac R. 13 § 62. alma
... fri t. fheola, Alex. 621. an t-én nó ghnathaighedh t.
a bproinne doibh, BNnÉ 79 § 154. conda tanic t. o Crist,
Lism. L. viii 25.

II anus: co lluid hi t. a chuirp, TBC² 1735 = con dechaid
dar t. a chuirp, TBC 3947. fuil na srona, no na timtirachta,
Rosa Ang. 18.17. nescoid arin timtiracht, 200.16. a tim-
paracht an othu[i]r, O'Gr. Cat. 270.30. ider in timperacht
┐ na huirghe, 271.2. na heigin go laidir do timperacht nec
comprime fortiter anum, Mackinnon Cat. 66.y.
see *do-imthiret.

egForm.p:
i, m. (*do-imthiret) servant, minister: gille
dano nó timtirid, Mon. Tall. 142.1. is timthirid tairise
do'n choimdid, PH 4203. mogæ et timthirthidi, Wb 8c11.
madgenatar á thimthirthidi, Ml 90b12. cenmothá fossu ┐
timthirthidi, TBC² 162. ba oen na timthirthite
she was
one of the servants, Lat. Lives 74.7. do na timtirithidib,
PH 5093. no-barn-aitchim, a thimthirige demain, 1852.
mar thimthiridh ┐ mar ionnstramuint, Parrth. Anma,
311.4. usci isin cailech ar tus icon temprid `when water is
being served in the beginning into the chalice by the server,'
Ir. Eccles. Rec. ii (1866) 172.19 (LB 251a14). ds. as adv.
(cf. Ped. ii 599.3): in t. gl. officialiter, Ml 53b20.

io, [n. ?] covering: damdabach na caladsciath
cona timthugu do lannaib óir, TTr.² 892. timthugach
(? leg. timthuga) oir, RC xliii 10.22.

side: do thin Trago Baili, RC xiii 222.37 = do taob
Thrágha Baile, MS. Mat. 473.31. tincur .i. taeb ecar, Laws
i 126.33 Comm. fo tin [.i.] fo taobh, iv 380.26.

eg.p: ? ni coimdi[g] t. mo tsamla, O'Dav. 581.

egForm.p:
(Only in etymological glosses on tinu, which is perhaps
from 1 tin, Plummer MS. notes). frisbert tinu a thoib .i. ro
frithbrudestar conar'bo thiug a thoeb, quia fit `tin' .i.
tiug nó moeth nó boc nó tosach, ut dicitur `tinns-
cital,' ACC § 101. tin .i. meith no bocc no maoth, ut dicitur,
frisbert tinu a taoib ┐ ni bi fri coilced tinca, H.3.18, 79. (O'C.
138). tin .i. bog, ut est frisbert ..., O'Dav. 1601. tin .i.
tosach no bunadh. tinnrem .i. tinnsgital, 1602. tin .i.
maoth nó meth nó bocc nó tosach nó tindscetal nó tinnrem,
O'Mulc. 871. Hence in B. na f. soft, easy: búc tion, ZCP
iii 378.12 = budc t., v 483.18.

o, ā (? 1 tin; cf. taebach) many-sided (?) : tuirid
na tuath t. trén, SR 6261. dar talmain tinaig, 8028. forsin
tracht tírimm t., 8112. a eír t. | tinghair niulu nime doghair,
ZCP viii 197 § 12.

eg.p: ? meth no eg fhirthinaig, YBL 175a1.

egForm.p:
u, m. vn. of tinaid. act of melting, vanishing: for
tinadh ┐ for tanughudh, CCath. 2372 n. ar ba ferr leo a
thinud oltas bethugud na n-Iudaide de
that it should be
wasted, Lism. L. vii. 3. tinfedh .i. tiniudh feadh .i. nemnigud
feadha, Auraic. 769. gabuis ... in chēir ag tionadh ┐ ag
legadh, Fl. Earls 34.18.

(inflexion not clear; see Ped. ii 648) melts, vanishes:
t. gl. euanescit, Sg. 4b6. tinsit a ndúine fo tráig | fillsit
glúine fo chombáig, SR 3465. ro thinai in snechta ... la
bréthir Patraic, Trip. 56.8. ro thinsat na cait o ro bo maten,
LU 8769 (FB). ro-thinastar focétoir ┐ dochuaid ar nemní,
Lat. Lives 91.2. tinaid failte inna mbrécaire, PH 6061.
tinait ┐ feodaigit fo cetoir, 4243. ceo atraiges fri re mbec
┐ tinas fo cetoir, 4659. ? To this: Borg Emna ro tetha,
Fél. Prol. 193 (but cf. Marstrander, Présents à nasale
infixée 14).

eg.p:
lam ceill comforbaidh co t. (.i. co ndib n-airtib),
LL 393a2. ? To this: ni moinech nach macaemda acht
ma tecma tindard talman, BB 278a5 = dind arradh talmhan,
BR 198.3.

egForm.p:
(*to-in-ás) growth: co trilis fuit dā lām ┐ co tinās
ulcha fair, Rawl. 147a51. is ed modh rogab ulcha th. do
